Artist and developer Temmie Chang, best known for work on Undertale and all five current Deltarune chapters, has released the third game in a short trilogy that's separate from Toby Fox's seminal RPGs, though they also feature Fox in the credits for melodies.

Chang shared Of the World, part three after Escaped Chasm and Dweller's Empty Path, over the weekend. It's playable in-browser through Itch.io, but it's recommended that you download the game to ensure your progress is saved following future updates.

"It is recommended to play Escaped Chasm and Dweller's Empty Path first," Chang advises.

Escaped Chasm is described as "A small little RPGmaker game about a lonely girl with a connection to another world that she sees in her dreams." Dweller's Empty Path is very similar, focusing mostly on "walking around and talking to NPCs and objects."

The third game in the series, which keeps the recognizable pixel art and exploration but seems to add more complex combat mechanics, has sparked quite a response so far. Chang's reveal post on Twitter has 1.8 million views, according to Twitter metrics. The game's YouTube trailer has over 330,000 views at the time of writing.

"Thank you for taking an interest in my little game!!" reads an Itch update from Change. "I'm once again blown away and surprised people have taken interest in my little games." Change adds, "Thank you again for playing, it really means a lot! I'm a little embarrassed by all the attention like this, but it is super appreciated nonetheless!"

Just days ago, we heard that Deltarune Chapter 6 is now "structurally complete" and work on Chapter 7 has "just started." Fox says, "Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence...!" So far, Deltarune has amassed a staggering 131,300 reviews on Steam, clocking in at 98% positive.

#3712. The Sunday Papers

The Sunday Papers is our weekly roundup of great writing about (mostly) videogames from across the web.

Sundays are for googling local purveyors of live Christmas trees, the sole upside of no longer having a cat being that you can once again enjoy the smell of chopped woodland without the risk of it poisoning a family member. Well, then again, I mean... empirically speaking, you're probably just assuming that your human loved ones haven't eaten spruce needles. Can you say for an absolute fact that they wouldn't?

Fortunately, while your nan is off having her stomach pumped, you can pass the time by reading some good words from this week.

First up is, if I'm honest, nepotism. But there's also no rule against the Sunday Papers including RPS staff when they're not writing for RPS, so in the interests of spreading understanding about games media's most underappreciated discipline, here's our own guides writer Jeremy Blum on the making of his (excellent) Castlevania: Belmont's Curse walkthrough.

Rockstar brought weather back to Leonida.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In my first 30 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6, I think I saw it rain once. And that was during a particularly gloomy main story mission where it felt like it was intentionally flipped on and not a serendipitous moment created by the game's weather system.

I was not alone in wondering what was up with the weather in Leonida. GTA 6 players have been confused by the lack of rain and fog since day one, especially after Rockstar boasted about the kind of storms and hurricanes it can create to Game Informer in September.

Apparently, the questioning was justified: The weather system was broken and should now be fixed in a new patch that went out today.

"Fixed an issue that resulted in weather not changing for extended periods," the patch notes say, confirming that, while some players witnessed changes in weather, it was not properly happening at the rate it was intended.

You don't partner with The Weather Channel to post exclusive pre-release screenshots of your game if the forecast is mostly sunny and not actually representative of Florida, the state with the most unpredictable weather in the US. GTA 6 has realistically detailed radio towers that left a TikTok guy who's worked on them in real life gobsmacked. It would've been bizarre if Rockstar neglected to put that kind of effort into a system normies like me would notice within a few hours.

The sun's reign is over and all the other meteorological conditions can take the spotlight. As someone who takes their time doing all the silly little daily routines in Jason and Lucia's life and abiding by traffic laws for the vibes, I'm excited to see how much the weather affects the mood. I'll just have to remember to be a little more discerning when chasing down one of GTA 6's cars to make sure I don't absolutely ruin the interior from a surprise storm.

NEOWIZ has signed a publishing partnership with Sweden-based studio Winterkeep Interactive for a new fantasy 4X strategy game described as a “new premium intellectual property,” the companies announced.

Winterkeep Interactive is led by Mattias Wiking, Petter Nallo, Karl Emdin, Frida Eriksson and Ola Enberg, and comprised of Paradox Interactive veterans whose previous credits include titles such as Stellaris, Crusader Kings II, Europa Universalis IV, Victoria 3, and other games.

#3709. GTA 6 players are being abducted by aliens and knocked out by Bigfoot

Grand Theft Auto 6 has only been out for a matter of hours, and players have already tracked down a UFO in the woods and a Bigfoot in the swamps.

The UFO encounter is a random night-time event in Kelly County, on a dirt road near the Starlet Motel safehouse east of Port Gellhorn. You'll need to have finished the game's first chapter, and it's most reliable after 2am in-game.

As word spread late yesterday (18th November), it seems the event will kick off if you find a car at the side of the road with its headlights flickering, its trunk open, and clothes strewn around it. Follow the trail into the trees towards a blue glow, and you'll catch a UFO beaming down on a woman before it drops her and flies off. Head back to her car, as she requests, and the UFO returns for you. You apparently black out and come round three days later, and a bronze trophy called The Truth Is Out There should unlock.

You can seemingly trigger the event as either Jason or Lucia, and it isn't needed for 100 percent completion.

And that's not the only close encounter you can expect, either. YouTuber Lazarbeam bumped into Bigfoot on the afternoon of 18th November, hours before the game launched in the UK, while one Reddit user reported that they weren't quite sure what they'd stumbled on, titling their post "I think I found Bigfoot".

Leonida's version of Bigfoot is actually the Skunk Ape, Florida's own swamp cryptid, and it can be found in the swamplands near Cottonmouth Lake in Mariana County as soon as free roam opens up. Listen out for a loud roar, then use Jason's tracking ability to follow it through the swamp. You may find it feeding on a deer carcass, while a second sighting has been reported south of Watson Bay.

Either way, the trail seemingly ends at a strange, human-like tree. Investigate it, and Jason blacks out, triggering a short cutscene in which the creature creeps up on him, as shown in this video. He later wakes near his vehicle, drenched in sweat. Save your ammo, though, as shooting at it won't do you any good.

Cryptids and aliens are, of course, something of a Rockstar tradition by this point. GTA 5's Mount Chiliad mystery kept players hunting for years, and Output Lag has already spotted two NPCs in a GTA 6 bar talking about goings-on there. Nobody has cracked a full Chiliad-style puzzle in the new game yet, but I'm sure that's just a matter of when, not if.

GTA 6 launched today on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, although some have been getting in on the action earlier as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first."

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

#3708. Undisclosed AI-generated music pulled from The Binding of Isaac Repentance+ update, as attempt to get satirical on GTA 6 launch day goes awry

Original creator Edmund McMillen said he "had no idea [the update] featured generated music in the daily run"

An update for The Binding of Isaac packed with wink wink, nudge nudge parody of GTA 6 has backfired rather spectacularly, with publishers Nicalis having to make some hasty modifications. This free addition to the Repentance+ version of the roguelike featured a Grand Terry Auto-inspired daily run, complete with cops, guns, and a soundtrack players soon highlighted as sounding AI-generated. Sure enough, Nicalis subsequently announced the "removal of generated music files" in response to the backlash.

The Repentance+ update went live on November 19th to coincide with GTA 6's release, and the music files had been yanked by Nicalis as of November 21st. In the interim, a Reddit user with the handle ShweetsStuff unearthed metadata pointing to AI tune generator Suno attached to some of the update's music files. Cue understandable questioning of why the DLC's Steam page hadn't had a disclosure of this genAI use slapped across it.

Original Binding of Isaac creator Edmund McMillen seems to have quickly ended up with inboxes full of folks asking him about what'd happened and demanding action. "Woke up to a shit show," he posted on the former Twitterverse on the 21st. Obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned."

Given the new build yanking the music went live later that day, McMillen's voice maybe only added to the chorus of complaints Nicalis were already aware of and facing. Either way, the songs are gone and Nicalis don't look to have said anything as of writing about whether they'll be replaced at some point down the line.

This isn't the first time a developer has considered using AI to generate songs designed to satirise or parody. In the case of Future? No Thanks! dev Paolo 'Molleindustria' Pedercini, the aim was partly to poke fun at disclosures, with people in the game's future society listening to AI-generated tunes that're corporately mandated to mention AI in the lyrics. Pedercini ended up deciding not to use AI-generated music in the final release.

On the face of it, while the effectiveness of using AI-generated songs to parody AI-generated songs is questionable, the argument for it seems stronger in a more focused satire like Future? No Thanks! than in the case of The Binding of Isaac having a GTA 6-related giggle. I've not listened to the Repentance+ update's AI tunes, but there's nothing obvious to indicate that their satirical job wouldn't have been done as well or better by Nicalis commissioning or otherwise employing someone to pen some entirely human-made ditties, that spoofed the nature of Large Stealy Wheely.

Perhaps the publishers will now go and do just that.

To steal the Declasse Vamos for Moses in GTA 6, you'll need to hunt around for the code to the garage

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The GTA 6 Declasse Vamos is a stunning pillarbox red muscle car that Moses wants you to pick up for him as one of the many side quests available in GTA 6. While some of Moses' targets are easy in-and-out type situations, others are a little trickier, and the Declasse Vamos heist, located just north of Grayson in South West Lummox County, is one of them.The GTA 6 Declasse Vamos itself is located in a locked garage next to a very interesting shack whose owners apparently love stealing a road signs. This is your hint to finding the garage door code, though it's not as hard as the mess of signs might make you think, as I'll share below.

The code for the garage in which you'll find the GTA 6 Declasse Vamos is 2727, as you can see on a couple of small tin signs mounted on the interior walls of the shack.

The entire building is covered floor to ceiling in metal signs, but if you have a good look around, there are at least two on the walls that feature this four-digit code, indicating that this is the number you need to gain access to the Declasse Vamos.

There are two residents here who'll be standing in your way, but now you've got the code, you could just stealth straight to the garage door, as this code is the same for everyone, unlike some of the GTA 6 safe codes. If you want to complete the mission yourself fully, though, you can knock out or kill the NPCs before entering the house and finding the code. As ever, there are a few items to pick up here, too, but it's not much.

For help on getting hold of some other GTA 6 cars, check out my guides on the GTA 6 Fast and Furious car, inspired by Paul Walker's (Brian O'Conner's) Mitsubishi Eclipse, the BF Bandito, which is another of Moses' targets, and Vanessa's Pink Porsche, the Growler, which is a secret find you can keep for yourself or sell on.

World of Warcraft: Forever now has more people playing each week than World of Warcraft has seen in 15 years, according to Blizzard.

"Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years!" executive producer and World of Warcraft vice president Holly Longdale posted. "Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever!"

Longdale was quoting a post from the official World of Warcraft account, which shared a batch of "By the Numbers" stats for the new edition.

Since it launched on 4th November, players have created 15,160,147 characters and 140,764 guilds, completed 1,480,343,357 quests, and defeated 9,786,925,806 enemies.

Another fun statistic for you! #WoWForever has more people playing weekly than we've seen in World of Warcraft in 15 years! Thank you all for joining us in Azeroth. We're doing this together, for Forever! 💙♾️ https://t.co/bMLQduLri2

#3705. Nvidia release hotfix for latest graphics card driver battering SSDs with excessive writes, but it looks like reverting may still be the better option

621.35 appears not to completely atone for 621.24's sins

Late last week, reports emerged of some folks having Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, needlessly write vast amounts of data to their PC's SSD, a bug that could affect the component's lifespan at a time when replacing SSDs certainly isn't cheap. The immediate short-term solution for affected users was to roll back to a previous driver, 621.01. Sadly it appears that might still be the best way to go despite Nvidia having released a hotfix.

The hotfix, driver version 621.35, was released on November 20th and as of writing is only available to download directly from the Nvidia website. It's designed to address one issue, this being that "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background".

"Since we have so many changes being checked in, we usually try to align driver releases with significant game or product releases," Nvidia wrote in their announcement of the hotfix. "This process has served us pretty well over the years but it has one significant weakness. Sometimes a change that is important to many users might end up sitting and waiting until we are able to release the driver. The fixes that make it in are based in part on your feedback in the Driver Feedback threads and partly on how realistic it is for us to quickly address them. These fixes (and many more) will be incorporated into the next official driver release, at which time the hotfix driver will be taken down.

"To be sure, these Hotfix drivers are beta, optional and provided as-is. They are run through a much abbreviated QA process. The sole reason they exist is to get fixes out to you more quickly. The safest option is to wait for the next WHQL certified driver. But we know that many of you are willing to try these out."

Unfortunately, it seems that based on some testing by users on r/Nvidia, the hotfix makes the situation with excessive SSD writing less bad than it is with 621.24, but doesn't eliminate the problem entirely. According to one of these users, 621.35 stops the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reduces the amount that's being written when the issue's at its peak, but doesn't prevent some excessive writing creeping in if hardware is left running for extended periods or left idling overnight.

Given that, rolling back to 621.01 still appears to be the most effective way of keeping the writes at an acceptable level while waiting for Nvidia to release a new driver than can permanently do away with the problem. One would hope it won't take too long, especially given the 621.24 driver still doesn't look to have been pulled offline so no one else grabs it prior to a fix arriving.

If you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's only writing a matter of MB or chunks of GB.

It's been a big week for videogames—or rather, videogame. Grand Theft Auto 6 is enjoying what may very well be the single greatest media launch in history, securing over $3.7 billion in launch sales. But as Rockstar enjoys its acclaim, other developers—like Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski—are professing some anxiety about releasing their own games in a post-GTA 6 world.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle," Sarzynski said on Bluesky over the weekend, joking that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled."

That news came as a surprise to Cyberpunk 2 lead writer Anna Megill, who replied with a baffled "But wait—"

Sarzynski was, of course, just goofing. But I'm sympathetic to any game dev who might be feeling an amount of apprehension about being measured against GTA 6's success, particularly when there's a genre overlap.

In Cyberpunk 2's case, however, CD Projekt is very much in its own lane: Cyberpunk is a different thematic setting, with entirely different systems and design goals. I'd hope that any reasonable person would think comparing the two is like comparing apples and oranges—particularly when the oranges reportedly had a production budget upwards of $1 billion.

In a follow-up post, Sarzynski acknowledged that each project is doing its own thing, while noting that GTA 6's example will benefit other game developers by serving as a source of creative inspiration.

"Seriously though, I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he said. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is: It expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed."

#3702. Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"

On bringing Thieves Guild up to snuff with the Haunted Cathedral and co

1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers advise new players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered, thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other, furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the "immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the process.

In the course of a wide-ranging interview about how they're reworking this most devious of Dark Projects, Nightdive producer Daniel Grayshon explained that the map changes are "more in terms of background tech", than altering the fundamental design or introducing details that oblige different strategies. "They've gone into these levels in a sensible way to fix some practical problems with them, like some issues where you might be able to climb up to a place that you shouldn't have been able to climb up before," he commented.

The Thief remaster team have taken more liberties, seemingly, with some of the Thief Gold maps. "Because some of the levels that were introduced in Thief Gold - they felt quite blocky and quite rushed, maybe, as you go through them," Grayshon explained. "But our team again, they've been able to go through and completely renovate some of these levels. The Opera House now feels in some parts like an actual Opera House, instead of a couple of blocky rooms. So I think players will really look at these and think, oh yeah, these kinds of details make sense, without it being too disruptive or too immersion breaking…"

"One particular - maybe people will consider infamous - level of the Gold package would be the Thieves Guild," Grayshon added. "The Thieves Guild is, if I were to sum it up kind of briefly, it is maybe two hours of walking through what feels like sewers, the same environment over and over again. There was no real visual distinction as to where you are in the level.

"So, we acknowledged pretty quickly that we need to go in and look at the Thieves Guild and fix it up, and what we've been able to do is texture it a lot more effectively. Give areas distinct looks, without compromising any of the gameplay again, like I mentioned. So we've put a bit more signposting around as well. Nothing that's going to be intrusive or immersion breaking again. Just kind of pointing the player in the right direction, as well as some other little things that I'm not going to spoil too much, but I think players will maybe appreciate the effort that we've done for this one."

In general, Nightdive's broad aim has been "bringing those Gold levels up to the quality of the original and then taking all of those levels and then bumping them up to the next level - almost Thief 2 levels of quality in its environment design, especially in some of the mansions, and some of the later levels," Grayshon said. "That's the level we were aiming for."

I have Several Thoughts about Grayshon's thoughts above (yes, people who dislike huffy armchair theory, this is your cue to skip to the comments). One is that I continue to dislike "immersion" as an ideal, though I recognise that many devs just use it as easy shorthand for a bunch of ways of doing art, sound and interface design. I think it often translates to uninvestigated enthusiasm for photorealistic fidelity and experiences that feel "smooth" and "engaging" enough to induce a kind of chemical trance. Many of the games I consider most valuable are cranky and unwilling and jarring, requiring you to think critically about the simulation rather than 'losing yourself' inside it. As regards the original Thief specifically, I enjoy how its nigh-magical stealth induces feelings of wavering dissociation, and keeps me guessing about the solidity of my own body.

Secondly, there's the age-old argument that if you're going to preserve a game faithfully, you should preserve what it did badly. The Thieves Guild is a legend among players, much as Blighttown is among Dark Souls players and the Library is among fans of Halo: Combat Evolved. You learn much about the methodology of Thief at large from the guild's stifling contours, and it's thrilling to witness a bunch of very smart designers take a swing at a concept and not quite connect. I'll try to hold onto that rousing sentiment, when I'm playing the remaster and struggling to remember where they hid that damn vase.

#3701. Infamous GTA 6 leaker CyberLeek is back, and this time the group claims to have leaked a full development build of the game

CyberLeek, the persona of a hacker group that was responsible for leaking GTA 6 gameplay before the game launched, has reappeared today, claiming to have released a development build of the final version of the game on its site. This new leak appears to be making good on a threat posted back in October, where the group stated its intent to release a full, playable build of the game.

Various social media accounts have visited the site and noted the size of the download offered by CyberLeek is, indeed 209GB. Eurogamer has seen the site and can confirm this is what the group has claimed, however I have been unable to verify the existence of any actual files. On the site, CyberLeek claims this build is from November 2026 - meaning it is very close to (if not the actual) release build. The 'executable file appears to be missing from the build, however, meaning you cannot actually - yet - get it up and running. CyberLeek is threatening to release this file at a later date, however.

"It is done," a statement from CyberLeek reads. "[Cyberleek] holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto 6, and it is going out by torrent. Now. Every file except one. The main executable is held on a countdown." CyberLeek says the executable will be released earlier than planned if its crypto token reaches a predetermined value. Many of the leaks to date have been related to a CyberLeek crypto scheme. Previously, it was estimated that the group cashed out at least £200,000.

What does all this mean? There's a very realistic chance that the game could be up and running on PC soon - undercutting Rockstar's unannounced PC release by a matter of months, if current rumours are to be believed. "This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps," the statement continues. "[CyberLeek] told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.

"If the Xbox build cannot be made to work and support holds, [CyberLeek] will work to get a PS5 build - a fallback, most likely never required. Either way: the Xbox build is going out. No double dipping for Take-Two/Rockstar." It seems these are not empty threats.

CyberLeek has been a thorn in Rockstar's side for a while now. The group initially claimed it took this action in the name of "Gamers' Rights", supposedly fighting for consumers in relation to the controversial discontinuation of game-discs and the digital-only future being pursued by game publishers. Rockstar has previously issued statements regarding the leaker, noting that the leaks are "heartbreaking" and that "this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time". Take-Two tried to subpoena Discord for information pertaining to the leaker's identity.

#3699. Nvidia reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO following alleged affairs, as US government support renders 'please give me my job back, go USA' a highly persuasive plea

Sexy leather jacket man's successor is exact same sexy leather jacket man, it turns out

Yep, he's back. Less than two weeks after Jensen Huang resigned from being CEO of Nvidia following reports of multiple affairs, the company's board have reinstated him "effective immediately".

"The board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang, after which the board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candour and ability to lead Nvidia," the company announced. "In the process of reaching its decision, the board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk."

"The board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," added recently appointed chairman Harvey Jones, who'll remain in the post following Huang's return. Colette Kress, who served as interim CEO during Huang's short break, will go back to just being chief financial officer.

"I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution," Huang declared. "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment."

Oh, and Nvidia's board added that the independent investigation they set in motion "in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort" will "proceed to conclusion". Huang "fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it", they noted.

Since resigning amid the scandal, Huang had made it clear he'd be open to returning to his post if the Nvidia board okayed it and had several powerful people either call for his reinstatement or declare they'd consider hiring him. "The country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy," one such advocate, US president Donald Trump, has reportedly posted to cursed hellcape Truth social. Huang is a "great patriot and national treasure", the Trumpeter added.

So, there you go. I'm not saying that you're totally immune to consequences for alleged actions that'd lose any normal person their job for far more than 11 days if you're mates with the American president, but it sure does look like that, doesn't it? Hope Nvidia didn't throw out any leather jackets Huang couldn't manage to carry out of the building with him.

#3697. Ubisoft says Assassin's Creed Jade is still alive as it merges two of its Creative Houses

Ubisoft has confirmed that while Assassin's Creed Jade - its mobile entry in the series - is still in development, its focus remains with console and PC.

Speaking during the earnings call for Ubisoft's first-half results, CFO Frédérick Duguet said mobile was "still an opportunity for the medium to longer term, with games such as AC Jade on Assassin’s Creed", according to a transcript of the call published by Investing.com.

"Looking at what we can see in terms of long-term financial return, in the mindset of having a stronger focus in terms of capital allocation and financial returns, we consider that we would rather put our resources on bigger opportunities," Duguet said. "Today, we can say that console and PC remain our core focus for our biggest franchises."

He added: "The focus is really to make sure that we come with strong growth on console and PC, and notably PC, which is a more dynamic platform than ever."

Ubisoft last confirmed its China-set mobile game was still in the works in March, when it was mentioned in the publisher’s Assassin's Creed: Into 2026 blog. Assassin's Creed now sits within Vantage Studios, Ubisoft's joint venture with Tencent, which launched last year.

Ubisoft's results also confirmed some more changes to the way the company is run, with the publisher saying its new operating model is "now fully in place". Creative Houses 3 and 5 have been combined under the leadership of Julien Bares "to leverage synergies between Live experiences across platforms".

All leadership roles across the Creative Houses are now filled, too. An external general manager has been appointed for Creative House 4 and is set to join in January 2027, though Ubisoft hasn't yet confirmed who. That follows September's appointment of 2K and Amazon Games veteran Christoph Hartmann to lead Creative House 2, home to The Division, Ghost Recon, and Splinter Cell, which was renamed Massive Entertainment at the same time.

Outside the Creative Houses, Motherbrain, the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI experiment Teammates, is now a subsidiary in its own right. It's working on "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds". A separate unit has also been set up to look after brands that don't belong to any of the Creative Houses.

Ubisoft says the new structure is already paying off, pointing to the commercial success of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced and renewed momentum for Rainbow Six Siege, which it says ranked among the top 10 games across Xbox and PlayStation for monthly active users over the half.

That said, the publisher nonetheless posted a net loss of €254.5 million for the first half of the year, with net bookings down 16.5 percent to €644.7 million.

The news comes just hours after Ubisoft confirmed 166 job cuts at its Montréal and Québec City studios, the latest in a year of layoffs. They're part of the "major organisational, operational and portfolio reset" that Ubisoft announced in January. That initial announcement was accompanied by the news of two studio closures - affecting its Halifax mobile and Stockholm teams - plus the cancellation of six projects, including the much-delayed Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake.

Since then, 105 jobs have been cut at Red Storm Entertainment, the Ubisoft studio behind the Ghost Recon series, and around 380 employees were reportedly laid off when the publisher's Winnipeg and Belgrade teams shut in June. In October, Ubisoft closed Trials developer RedLynx and downsized its Singapore Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced team, impacting a total of approximately 120 employees. Amid all this, Ubisoft developers have been on strike in response to the publisher's sweeping layoffs.

On the weekend, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

Following his guilty plea, Arion Kurtaj was given a seven-year sentence but released "on license" with a warning and restrictions to his online activity..

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A BBC report says Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who was given an indefinite sentence in hospital in 2023 because he kept hacking into things or expressing intent to, has been released with a stern warning not to do it again.

Kurtaj was sentenced to seven years in prison, according to the report, but was released on license—similar to parole in North America—the same day, with his hospital stay and time in prison while awaiting retrial credited as time served. He was given a five-year "Serious Crime Prevention Order" restricting his allowable online activity, including bans on using Telegram and Discord.

"Kurtaj knew what he was doing when he carried out these crimes and has finally admitted his involvement," Detective Inspector Mike O'Sullivan of the City of London Police said following Kurtaj's sentencing and release. "We hope this case serves as a lesson that these types of acts will not be tolerated.

"Although cyber crime is borderless, we will seek to utilise the co-operation of partner agencies and international law enforcement to ensure that offenders are brought to justice no matter where they offend from."Kurtaj carried out hacks against multiple companies when he was 16 and 17 years old, including Microsoft, Samsung, Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals.

But it was his hack of Rockstar and leak of GTA 6 materials more than a year before it was formally revealed, that earned him notoriety, not least because of how it was carried out: While under police protection in a Travelodge hotel room, using an Amazon Fire Stick and a mobile phone.

A psychiatric assessment determined that Kurtaj had "acute autism," and that he "continued to express the intent to return to cybercrime as soon as possible" while he was in custody. That led to his hospital sentence, but earlier this year he was found fit to stand trial and subsequently pleaded guilty to all charges.

That struck me as odd—why plead guilty to crimes carried out at a time when your mental state was such that a court decided you required multiple years of institutionalization?—but this may be the answer: Kurtaj, now 21, is a free man. The judge on the case told Kurtaj he is "a very talented young man," but also warned him: "Don't let this happen again."

#3694. Blizzard wants to "get rid" of best-in-slot items in World of Warcraft: Forever by introducing situationally strong gear

"BIS is not a good thing for a game that's supposed to be about role-playing."

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

"I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon said. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different."

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list."

Moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

It's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm currently ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

The Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

GTA 6 is a massive game, and it might take you over 100 hours to beat

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

How long it takes you to beat GTA 6 is going to depend a lot based on how you play it. It's a huge game, so don't expect to get it done in fewer than 40 hours, but you might be able to get somewhat close to that if you're really rushing. However, for most GTA 6 players, completing open world activities and exploring is going to take up lots of time outside of doing main missions, so you're looking at putting in well over 50 hours to roll the credits. If you want to know more, I've broken down the length of GTA 6 in more detail below with some estimated completion times.

Playing all GTA 6 missions across the game's five chapters is a big undertaking that will keep you occupied for many hours. The writer of GamesRadar+'s GTA 6 review, Josh West, reckons it will take most players anywhere between 60 and 80 hours to complete the main story and roll the credits.But that's still assuming you're doing some open world exploration too, and, from my experience, it's often impossible to avoid that. In fact, the amount of time spent engaging with extra activities will have a big impact on your final time, which should be around these estimates depending on how you play:

If you're solely focused on the main story and getting it done quickly, you can shave off quite a lot of time, even getting below 50 hours. Bear in mind that you'll be missing out on quite a lot of the game by playing this way. A big part of the fun of GTA 6 is cruising around Leonida and doing all sorts of activities and bumping into bizarre encounters.

On the other end of the spectrum, if you're fully or even just partly committed to attaining 100% completion of GTA 6, you will be spending well over 100 hours playing. There are tons of side-mission chains to complete, unique activities to participate, and collectibles to find all over the map, so finding all of that, even with help from out GTA 6 guides, is a mammoth undertaking.

#3691. Finally, some former Valorant and Sky devs have answered the call for a Peak-style platformer about throwing a cat through a hole in spacetime

It's embarrassing that we had to wait this long

As a mature and sophisticated artform, videogames offer answers to many of life's important questions, such as "how many spaceships is too many spaceships?" (a trick question, obviously) or "which 12th century BC civilisation was better at playing Age of Empires 2?" Lately, I have been wrestling with the enigma of how I should transport a sleeping cat in a snowglobe up a psychedelic mountain. According to Whisk, I should phone a friend.

In this first-person co-op platformer - created in Unreal Engine, with both online multiplayer and splitscreen support - you and a mate play Luna and Foam, two rock-hopping magic children with nothing better to do than lob hermetically sealed felines through tears in reality itself. Egad! Apparently the cats are fine with this. You'll have to work together to traverse astral watercolour landscapes, hurling and catching the kitty while trying not to tumble into the abyss.

You can also catch each other's arms and haul each other onto safe ground, which puts this in approximately the same bracket as the well-liked Peak. Other Neat Tricks include bouncing the starry-eyed moggies from soap bubbles, swinging from strands of green snot (?), and springboarding from tornadoes.

The cats remain blissfully unconscious throughout, smiling in their slumber right up to the point when you crack their crystal prisons. If you're familiar with cats, the penalty for breaking their domes may seem rather mild. I was hoping for something along the lines of Peter Puppy having a rage-out in Earthworm Jim.

Would it surprise you to learn that one or more of the people working on Whisk is a former developer of Sky: Children of Light, the open world swoop 'em up from thatgamecompany? I imagine you might not consider that startling – the two games both look a little like the result of somebody inhaling burnt banana skins. But you might be giddier to hear that one or more of the Whisk devs is also a veteran of Riot's Counter-Strike descendant Valorant. I'm pretty sure Valorant doesn't have any cat-throwing, but I'm prepared to be proven wrong.

It's coming to Steam early access early in 2027, and there's a demo on Steam right now with eight levels and 10 cats to "rescue". People are already bragging in the forums about their leaderboard placements – monsters!

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting.

The estimates come from data-tracking company Sensor Tower (spotted by VGC), which has been watching GTA 6 pre-orders closely for weeks, updating estimates daily based on (unspecified) data that it collects.

Should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6.

So far, Rockstar has said nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent company Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. Reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". #3687. "Don't let this happen again": GTA 6 hacker who pleaded guilty to 2022 Rockstar Games breach released under supervision

Case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online", according to City of London Police

A hacker who pleaded guilty to the 2022 hacking breach of Rockstar Games, which resulted in a bunch of mid-development clips of GTA 6 in action leaking onto the net, has been released under supervision. The hacker, Arion Kurtaj, has also a five year long serious crime prevention order which will restrict what he can do online.

The BBC report that Kurtaj has been released on licence after serving most of a seven-year sentence. On licence means his release is subject to a number of conditions. According to the UK Government website, the exact nature of these conditions varies from person to person and case to case, as they've got be "considered necessary and proportionate". However, things like needing not to commit any more crimes, not travel abroad, and live under the supervision of community offender manager are cited as part of a set of "standard licence conditions" outlined by the government site.

Kurtaj has also been given a serious crime prevention order to run for five years, restricting his activity online. It includes bans from using both Telegram and Discord.

According to the BBC, the judge told Kurtaj Yyou are a very talented young man," and warned him: "Don't let this happen again." City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online".

Kurtaj pleaded guilty on November 16th at Woolwich Crown Court to the 2022 Rockstar Games hack, as well as a number of others he carried out with the hacking gang Lapsus$ while aged 16 and 17. Now aged 21, he was previously sentenced to stay in a secure hospital indefinitely, due to the severity of his autism, but was subsequently deemed fit to stand trial.

90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 were flung online by the 2022 hack, with Rockstar having refused to cooperate with Kurtaj's demand via an internal Slack channel that the company contact him on massaging app Telegram within 24 hours. Rockstar claimed the breach cost them $5m million to recover from, in addition to staff having to waste thousands of hours.

Earlier this year, GTA 6 suffered yet another leak, with a hacker or hackers going by 'Cyberleek' posting various videos of the game in action. Rockstar and parent company Take-Two quickly sprung into action, taking down videos, filing subpoenas, and issuing a statement that called the leak "heartbreaking".

Cyberleek has since claimed to have lobbed a near-complete Xbox build of GTA 6 onto the net, while withholding a main executable file they threatened to release subsequently. Online sources claim the executable has now also been leaked, though this has not been independently verified.

#3684. Total War: Warhammer 40,000 breaks the game into star system mini-campaigns, each with their own stories and objectives

"We want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy."

There is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

In an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

The star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do."

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

As you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

On the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

"Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that."

Total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

All the endings (and a couple variations) for GTA 6 we've seen so far.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Obviously, massive spoilers follow for GTA 6 endings!

There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and while we haven't experienced them all personally here at PC Gamer, the gaming community has been sharing them around for anyone curious about what they may have missed.

The ending you get depends on the choices you make during the final GTA 6 story mission, but also depends on how you handled Jason and Lucia's romance and criminal profiles throughout the game, so seeing every version of the ending would mean not just playing the ending multiple times, but having different playthroughs of the game altogether.

There are a couple of endings that I don't consider "different" from each other but do have some differences leading up to them, which I'll explain below. There may also be additional endings we haven't seen yet, so we may update this guide in the future.

In the bridge endings, Jason and Lucia have defeated Mendez and his squad and gotten the hard drive back from Georgio's penthouse and escaped. They drive to Cal's place in Key Lento, but discover he has been compromised. They drive to the bridge, but the cops have set up a roadblock and have the couple trapped. Lucia wants to keep going, but Jason suggests they jump off the bridge and swim for it.

A choice comes up on the screen: "Swim For it" or "No Surrender."

Jason and Lucia try to run the roadblock and are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, we see that their son Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, their lawyer, Abe, brings the money to Lucia's aunt. Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children in a much bigger house than the other No Surrender ending.

Choosing "Swim for it" presents an additional choice. When Jason gets out of the car, Lucia can choose to "Exit" the car with him, or change her mind by not choosing it.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. They both exit the car without holding guns. Lucia jumps, but Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Lucia signs a deal for immunity while Jason goes to prison. Lucia gets a job in a diner. Lucia takes Tomas to meet Jason in prison, but he can only see his son through a glass divider.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. Jason exits the car with a gun, but Lucia changes her mind and stays in the car. The police open fire and Jason and Lucia are both shot to death. Tomas lives with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it, Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Two years later, Lucia uses the savings account to get Jason freed from prison. Lucia goes to the prison to pick up Jason. Jason meets Tomas and holds his hand.

If you don't have a strong relationship between Jason and Lucia, there is a different ending location: the base of Georgio's tower. In these endings, the couple never makes it to the bridge. You can also choose to break up the couple, either as Jason or as Lucia, as you begin the mission Protective Custody.

After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront the couple at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia has a choice to "Stay down" or "Defend Jason". She stays down and watches Jason die. Lucia is arrested, signs a deal, and visits Tomas at her aunt's house. Lucia then leaves Tomas with her aunt, takes out a gun, and continues her life of crime by preparing to rob a diner.

After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront them at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia chooses "Defend Jason" and fights the cops. They die together.

On the way down to ground level at the tower, Jason decides to run. Lucia is arrested and signs the deal, then lives with her aunt and Tomas while working in a diner. One night there's a knock on the door and she finds a bag of cash on the porch. We see Jason driving away with... Rocco the drug-sniffing dog from earlier in the game. Sure, that might as well happen.

How to get this ending (sourced by GamingwithTZ on YouTube):

Jason and Lucia make a deal with Mendez after defeating him. Once they have the hard drive, they're surrounded by cops at the bottom of the tower. Mendez arrives and takes them away in his car, then drives them to the swamp. Later in the credits, we see two skulls in the swamp, side-by-side, with a bullet hole in each.

Note: You may need a specific criminal profile for this ending. I tried to take the deal (as Lucia) in one of my ending playthroughs, but Jason shot Mendez anyway. I had both Jason and Lucia at "Professional" level criminal profiles. This ending was not available to me. Speculation, but this ending may only be available if you don't have "Professional" as your criminal profiles.

There are potentially (and almost certainly) more endings to GTA 6. There are still a few combinations of all the different variables, including your romance level, criminal profile level, amount of money saved, and the choices you make during the final mission, that we haven't seen yet.

We'll update this guide if the community finds more endings.

Chris started playing PC games in the 1980s, started writing about them in the early 2000s, and (finally) started getting paid to write about them in the late 2000s. Following a few years as a regular freelancer, PC Gamer hired him in 2014, probably so he'd stop emailing them asking for more work. Chris has a love-hate relationship with survival games and an unhealthy fascination with the inner lives of NPCs. He's also a fan of offbeat simulation games, mods, and ignoring storylines in RPGs so he can make up his own.

#3682. Might and Magic meets, er, paper in sunny new RPG Rise of Furax, a turn-based island tale that is entirely drawn by hand

Is that you, Mr Sneeze? What have they done to you, boy?

Literal decades ago, I tried to make a first-person RPG in HyperCard. I got as far as a fateful town gate confrontation before hitting the cap on slides for the shareware version. I mention this because new, 100% "hand-drawn" first-person dungeon crawler Rise of Furax is uncannily redolent of my long-lost HyperCard game.

This risks being a) a terrible indictment of the game's visual direction, and b) an insinuation that developers Rap2h are dastardly rip-off artists, so let me elaborate that c) I think Rise of Furax looks far, far lovelier than my lousy primordial hypermedia confection and d) it is a legally distinct creation. That unfinished HyperCard concept never left the confines of a Macintosh Performa that is even now rusting on a riverbed. If only I'd pitched it somewhere, I'd probably be a MILLIONAIRE by now. A million pounds is still a lot of money, right? Anyway, here's a teaser video for Rise of Furax.

The plot setup here is thusly: some apocalypse cult is raising havoc on three islands off the coast of Rivelune. Five heroes – a snake minstrel, a rhino barbarian, a badger knight, a goat sorcerer and… whatever the hell critter that monk is - have been sent to investigate the whole "world is ending" sheebang and do a little levelling.

As in the very first Might and Magic, you steer the party as one, moving around a grid map. Combat is turn-based and there are "secrets, puzzles, and hidden items everywhere". Also schmürpfs. These confuse me even more than the monk character. They look like angry green omelettes. Any pointers? I googled the word and the closest match I could find was Swiss footballer Pascal Schürpf, who appears neither green nor egg-based.

"Every element, from sprites to textures, was hand-drawn on paper," promises the Steam page. It's out April 2027. There's no demo as yet nor even a proper trailer, but god I enjoyed looking at this, in a week otherwise full of screenshots of, like, suggestive scallion distribution in GTA 6. I should finish that HyperCard game. I still remember which river I threw the Performa into.

#3681. UK Prime Minister won't be playing GTA 6, government says, while hailing Rockstar Games a "British success story"

Grand Theft Auto 6's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full".

"Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it."

Downing Street went on to address the issue of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters".

The leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns. "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else."

GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

This state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

Rockstar is reportedly looking to adapt Red Dead Redemption for the big and small screens.

According to The Ankler, Rockstar has been "throwing around a purchase price of more than $100 million minimum for licensing rights" to the Red Dead Redemption franchise with the hopes of making a movie or a TV show.

In Red Dead Redemption, the player controls a former outlaw named John Marston whose wife and son are held hostage by the government in exchange for Marston's bounty hunter services. It's an open-world game that's set in the year 1911 and has some horror elements (and some weird things happen when you let the game idle for a bit, depending on what you're doing in that moment). Red Dead Redemption 2, a prequel to the first game, was released in 2018.

A Red Dead movie has been in demand for quite some time, dating all the way back to its 2010 release (with Brad Pitt initially tapped by fans as the perfect John Marston). Jack Black even said that Red Dead had a "better story than The Last of Us" and therefore deserved its own live-action adaptation.

Given that Far Cry, God of War, and Assassin's Creed are all in the works, and the fact that The Last of Us received some Emmy nominations... I'd say now is as good a time as any to turn your blockbuster video game into a live-action something or other.

#3678. Star Wars: Galactic Racer studio "didn't dream" Biddy Blas would be as popular as he is

"He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly."

Fuse Games, the developer of Star Wars: Galactic Racer, has said it "didn't dream" the pod racing game's background character Biddy Blas would become as popular as he has.

Since Galactic Racer's release in October, Blas - who resembles a short, humanoid crocodile (officially a crocin) - has become a viral sensation. The combination of his unexpected swagger and ridiculous high-pitched Huttese monologues - performed irresistibly by actor Richard Summers-Calvert - have made him a fan favourite, especially his catchphrase "scrib doon" (which means "write it down").

"Here's a name for you, amateur!" Blas tells the player upon meeting them, albeit in Huttese. "Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!"

Fuse Games shared a comment from Biddy Blas creator and Galactic Racer narrative designer Ren Alex-Rose about the character's success. "We always suspected Biddy Blas would be a popular member of the Galactic League, but we didn't dream of just how popular he'd become," Alex-Rose said.

"He was an incredibly enjoyable character to build, from our early ideation of a small, angry non-human character (who we lovingly referred to as our cast's 'chaos goblin') to recording his sometimes-absurdist dialogue with Blas' voice actor, who took the crocin to a whole new level.

"It's been great watching Biddy Blas emerge into his assured self, as well as seeing the community embrace him for it. He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly."

Blas' breakout success was praised by Lucasfilm producer Craig Derrick, who said his social feeds were filled with posts about Galactic Racer, though mostly about Biddy Blas. And the enthusiasm actor Richard Summers-Calvert was greeted with during October's MCM Comic-Con in London, which I attended, was palpable. There's a nice video of him doing Blas' voice on Instagram.

Star Wars: Galactic Racer was awarded a full five stars in Eurogamer's review. "Both a surprisingly fun Roguelite campaign and a racing treat for Criterion fans, this is just wonderful stuff," wrote Christian Donlan.

#3677. Think you know games? That we liked? This year? Then join the RPS Advent Calendar Guessing Game 2026

Turn your games-of-the-year conjecture into fabulous prizes

Ho ho ho, the RPS Advent Calendar 2026 is... not ready yet. We haven’t written the words, and I keep forgetting to unblur that new picture of Horace (drawn by the reliably talented Amanda Flagg). But while drag our lumpen feet on the business of deciding our favourite games this year, RPS readers have begun plotting, and scheming, and apparently in some cases, spreadsheeting. That’s right: the Advent Calendar Guessing Game has returned, and is open right now for keen participants.

If you’re unfamiliar with this grand tradition – which is once again being run by extra-lovely reader Aerothorn on the RPS Discord – then here’s a quick rundown. You, the reader, take a guess at the 24 games we’ve chosen to hide behind Horace’s wall of advent doors this year, finalising your list before the calendar launches on December 1st. Once all games are revealed, those with the most accurate guesses shall bask forever in the glory of their triumph, and also bag some free access to the RPS Supporter programme. 3rd place wins a three-month subscription, 2nd place wins six months, and the 1st place Guesser Supreme wins a full year of Supp perks.

Be warned, though, that victory will demand a sharp mind and an impeccable memory. Or, at the very least, a willingness to go back through our reviews and What Are We Playing This Weekend posts, to remind yourself which games have taken our fancies these past twelve months. Anecdotally, I think we’ve been slightly better at actually writing about our favourites in 2026 than we were for last year’s calendar, which should hopefully make for an easier Guessing Game. If also, perhaps, a more competitive one?

You can read up on the full game eligibility rules, start discussing your picks, and submit your guesses by joining the #2026-advent-calendar-guessing-game channel in the RPS Discord linked above. Note that you don’t need to correctly guess the position of an included game to earn a point for it, only its presence in the list, though you should specify which game you think will earn the coveted Day 24 door – our overall top game of the year, essentially – as this detail will serve as one of the tiebreakers in the event of a draw.

Thanks again to Aerothorn for setting this up, and good luck to all who participate! Here’s one hint, for free: we didn’t have Sin, Oisin, and Jeremy P voting for the Advent Calendar after having them for the RPS 100, so don’t rely too much on the latter for inspiration. Sorry, Unbeatable.

Deborah Ann Woll said she felt "totally unbothered" by the small but vocal subset of gamers who were upset by the upcoming God of War: Laufey, and apparently she meant it—because today Amazon MGM Studios announced that she's going to play the same role in the live-action God of War series coming to Prime.

Just as in God of War: Laufey and its predecessor, God of War: Ragnarok, Woll—best known for playing Karen Page in Marvel's Daredevil, Defenders, and Punisher TV series, as well as a lengthy stint on True Blood as Jessica Hamby—will portray Faye, wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus.

"Faye’s abrupt passing sets in motion the events of God of War," the announcement says. "Along their journey, Kratos and Atreus discover secrets about Faye that make them wonder how well they truly knew her at all."

It's been a bumpy road for the God of War series. It was first reported in 2022, but started over from scratch two years later after the showrunner and executive producers quit. We got our first look at Ryan Hurst as Kratos earlier this year—not very impressive, but we all had the same initial impression of Henry Cavill as Geralt and that worked out well—but then Hurst had to be recast because of an on-set injury; Dave Bautista now has the lead role. Child actors Callum Vinson and Island Austin, who played Atreus and Thrud, were also recast.

God of War: Laufey is set to launch on May 20, 2027, but sadly is a PlayStation 5 exclusive, a state of affairs that seems likely to endure given Sony's recent strategy shift. The God of War live action series on Prime has been ordered for two seasons, but a release target hasn't been announced.

The GTA 6 Schafter v12 is not what you might think, which is what makes this theft tricky at first

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

If you're having trouble heisting the GTA 6 Schafter v12 for Raul, it's easier than you might think. The problem is that you've gotten used to stealing cars for Moses in GTA 6 Chapter 1, but now you're working for Raul, and his jobs are a little more... unusual. So, if you're driving away from the scene of the crime in a hot new motor, police on your tail, wondering why you're being told your job's not done, here's where you might be going wrong when trying to steal the Schafter v12 in GTA 6.

If you're struggling with this mission, the problem is most likely that you're stealing the wrong car. You should be looking for the shabby green car parked under the canopy with its trunk roof missing.

Having been keeping an eye out for so many nice cars by this point, be it for yourself, for Moses, or for Raul, you're lulled into a false sense of security. You go into this mission all guns blazing, literally, thinking you know what's up and that you don't need to waste time Wainking it. That stunning muscle car with the growling exposed engine and massive exhausts must be the car you're after, right? Wrong. Clearly placed here to lead you astray on purpose, that's actually the strangely reasonably priced Imponte Bloodbath Phoenix, so I recommend heading back to the area and taking that one for yourself later. For the Car Service mission, however, you'll need to drive away in the crumbling Benefactor Shafter v12.

Other than that, the only trouble you'll meet with this mission is the same as ever: a few criminals with weapons ready to be drawn. The best way to complete this one is to head onto the roof from round the back of the gated area before taking them all out with a silenced handgun, which I recommend for most small-to-medium heists at this stage.

If you're looking for more cars to steal for yourself, make sure you pick up the Paul Walker GTA 6 car, inspired by the 1995 Fast and Furious Mitsubishi Eclipse. And don't skip over the pink Porsche in GTA 6, which you can only get if you pay attention in Chapter 2.

#3674. 28 years later, grizzled XCOM-style WW2 tactics game Soldiers at War gets a fresh tour of duty on modern PCs

I realise "28 years later" suggests there are zombies - there are no zombies

Prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a new version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO series, except that it's set during World War 2. I don't believe they had Chryssalids back then. Pretty sure grandpa never mentioned any Chryssalids.

Originally developed by Random Games and published by Strategic Simulations, Inc, the game consists of 18 main scenarios spanning D-Day, Monte Cassino and Cherbourg. There's a mission editor, too, and some standalone extra skirmishes. In each scrap, you pick eight men to undertake such feats as raiding V2 sites and hijacking disabled tanks, drawing on a dizzying range of individual soldier actions. Your squaddies level up with experience, and you can equip them with flamethrowers and bazookas. Among the key differences from X-COM is that there's no morale system - your men will never defy orders. Nor is there an overarching base/Geoscape layer.

"This edition updates Soldiers at War to run smoothly on modern Windows systems, delivering improved compatibility and performance," promises the GOG page (it's also on Steam). "The game now supports 1280x720 widescreen resolution, with rendering improvements for smoother drawing." There are cloud saves and Achievements, too, for today's soldier is not content with merely laying down their life for their country. They must also unlock some percentage-based virtual trophies in the process.

I remember Strategic Simulations, Inc mostly for working on two games in the Close Combat series, but they developed and published a shedload of other strategy games and wargames before their eventual parent company Ubisoft retired the brand in the noughties. As for Random Games – hold the phone, those guys also made the original Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate!

#3673. GTA 6 players are already pulling off high-flying tricks and other impressive stunts, just days after launch

One of the best things to emerge from Grand Theft Auto over the years has been the community's truly spectacular stunts: players soaring under bridges, leaping across buildings, and more. And with GTA 6's release this week, we've seen the first signs of the trend continuing in a brand-new world.

This TikTok video by user Gstitz from early in GTA 6, for instance, claims to be the "world's first" demonstration of a Mallard flying sideways between a narrow gap in a large building. It takes several attempts, but they eventually pull off the stunt without crashing or broken parts.

Another video from Hazardous is a more grounded (literally) look at Grand Theft Auto 6, and shows the YouTuber flinging motorbikes and cars around the map as they explore promising high-risk jumps. Some of these locations are tied to in-game challenges, so there are certainly breadcrumbs placed by Rockstar to encourage such ventures.

Granted, these are far from the truly absurd stunts we've seen in prior Grand Theft Auto games. But as a firing gun for the wider community, it's a great start. They're also among the most impressive things we've seen in GTA 6's opening week.

It's doubtless been an eventful few days though. Players have been entranced by the slapstick violence and in-game social media. Even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has praised the game, despite not having time to actually play it. Eurogamer editor-in-chief Chris Tapsell also came away impressed, lauding it in his five star GTA 6 review.
