#3607. Mass Effect: Universe Writer Says BioWare Spent A ‘Long And Laborious’ Time On Making Sure It Handled ME3’s Endings In A Way That ‘Wouldn’t Piss Everyone Off’

Mass Effect fans are still lobbying in an effort to ensure thereâs a future for the series and for the work BioWare did on Mass Effect: Universe before the studio was shut down by publisher EA last month, but unless something comes of that, the canceled fifth RPG will remain just a dream for fans to ponder. More information about what BioWare was cooking has trickled out as some who worked on it speak frankly about the game that might have been, but. many of those folks are still under NDAs and canât talk openly about it., They can, however, at least offer some insight into what the team was thinking, and those people include Catherynne M. Valente, the author of the novel Mass Effect Andromeda: Annihilation Â and a writer on Universe. She held a Reddit AMA talking about her work on the series and revealed some interesting facts about where BioWareâs head was at when it comes to handling Mass Effect 3âs divergent endings.

Though we donât know much about how Universe would have handled whether players chose to destroy synthetic life, take control of the Reapers, or achieve Synthesis, leaks suggest that the game would have accounted for all of those possibilities somehow. According to Valente, ensuring that Universeâs handling of the endings âwouldn’t piss everyone offâ was one of BioWareâs big priorities. Despite years of fairweather fans saying BioWare should âjust make Destroy canon and move on,â that wasnât the route the studio wanted to take.

I don’t think it’s being naughty to say I (and not only me, but I did a lot on it) worked specifically, and for a very long and laborious time, on handling the endings in a way that wouldn’t piss everyone off, at least not piss them off completely, that wouldn’t make them feel like nothing mattered, wouldn’t privilege any one kind of player over another, but also allow us, somehow, to actually write a coherent story going forward, within the limits of having to do it in a playable mainstream video game and not a post-modern 3000 page novel.

Not for nothing, guys, but that’s kind of a tall fucking order. Part of the reason it took so long and Andromeda was in Andromeda is that figuring out an elegant solution to that problem turns out to be really hard. An elegant solution that we can do with current game tech, that will be approved by higher-ups, that doesn’t take over the whole game and make actually telling a story impossible…it takes a long time, and it’s not obvious how best to pull it off when you’re the people who bear responsibility for pulling off one of, if not the, hardest nut to crack in game writing.

And it’s become really clear that it’s impossible to make the gaming community completely happy with anything no matter how hard you try, especially the ME endings that were so controversial, yet people feel so strongly about their own choices. We burned out so many valuable neurons going up against that problem. I know so many people think it’s easy, just make Destroy canon and move on, but consider that, for example, I feel as strongly about Synthesis as others do about Destroy. And everyone feels strongly about choices mattering. Do you really think there is a single solution that would have satisfied everyone? In a video game?

But we did our best, and I think we landed in a good place. There wasn’t one single solution, but several working together, and unfortunately I can’t say any more than that.

I remember laughing ruefully once and thinking god, if I’d known when I finished ME3 that I’d be one of the people who had to find the mops and buckets to clean up that mess…

But as I’m saying a lot: yes, there was an answer, yes, I know it, as least inasmuch as I know what it was when I was working there, because part of it was my job, and we tried our damnedest to do right by the story and the fandom. That room was full of ambition and enthusiasm, and I don’t think it could have been in better hands. We knew all the discourse on the endings, of course we did, and I do think as a fan I would have been happy with the solution (at least what it was when I left) if I booted up the game having had nothing to do with it.

And I asked myself that at the end of everything I did: If I could go back to being just a fan, would I be happy with this?

Itâs nice to hear this sentiment again because I feel like the recent push for creators to just select one ending to make âcanonâ when creating sequels to choice-driven stories is more of a fan-driven impulse than it is a creator one. Often it feels rooted in a desire for more of a thing one likes at any cost, rather than in maintaining the integrity of the seriesâ role-playing and fiction, and usually in these situations, developers arenât looking for an easy way out. BioWare certainly wasnât, at least. Even during pre-release interviews for Dragon Age: The Veilguard, the studio was pretty adamant that it would rather not reference previous game choices than undermine them, though that would be impossible in a Mass Effect game set in the Milky Way after Mass Effect 3, given the galaxy-wide ramifications of the choices you make in that game.

Whatever Universeâs ambitions might have been for acknowledging all of Mass Effect 3âs endings, Valente also emphasized that the game wasnât done and that even the solutions the team was considering at this stage of development might not have been the ones used in the final game if it hadnât been canceled in favor of Star Wars Battlefront III.

âYou have to remember the game wasn’t done,â she wrote. âThings changed all the time, even week to week, and who knows where and how the things I worked on or saw others work on would have ended up in the final game. It’s forever frozen where it was when EA pulled its Renegade Interrupt, but that doesn’t mean that’s what it would have been without it.â

For now, Mass Effect fans are rallying around the #SaveMassEffect campaign that has amassed over 330,000 signatures in a Change.org petition, and has been putting billboards promoting the cause up in places like Times Square. Earlier this month, Canadian fans were able to successfully put forth a petition to be heard by the Canadian House of Commons, arguing that the Canadian government should help assist laid-off BioWare workers in buying the studio and its IP from EA, though any such deal would require the publisherâs cooperation.

Warning! Spoilers ahead for Season 9, Episode 7 of FBI, “Posterity,” streaming now with a Paramount+ subscription.

Over the last few years, FBI has seen a surprising amount of cast changes in such a short amount of time. Just last season, the CBS procedural said goodbye to Emily Alabi not long after she joined the cast, and Juliana Aidén Martinez was then brought on. After a recent update on the procedural pointed towards another exit on the 2026 TV schedule, I had to ask one star all about it, and they totally get why I have questions.

Earlier in this season of FBI, John Boyd’s Stuart Scola revealed that wife and baby mama Nina Chase (Shantel VanSanten) had been offered the chance to lead her own task force in San Diego. Despite some hesitation, Scola ultimately tells her she should take it, and last week’s episode, “Posterity,” saw Nina getting ready for the big move. After some thinking, Scola told her he was going to put in a transfer to move to California with her, even if it would take a while.

That development led me, and likely many fans, to worry that another exit could be coming and that we might say goodbye to Scola in the near future. However, Boyd told CinemaBlend what’s really going on and sought to ease concerns:

I mean, look, as far as I know, there's no plans for any major changes, but I think that's a perfectly natural question to have. But really what's happening is exploring the character in a relationship in a very real way of something that we haven't yet tried with this couple, which real couples go through, all the time in life, which is career changes and geographics and movement. And what does it mean to love someone and let them go, ask them to stay, give up your thing?

Boyd's comments seem to point to the writers simply wanting to shake things up for Nina and Scola in a way they've never done before. The actor also told us this:

It's sacrifice and change, and it makes them super relatable. So, that's the story we're telling for now, but it's perfectly fine to kind of, hopefully, tease the idea of certain characters not being around anymore to see if people really love them.

I’m relieved to know that Boyd’s not going anywhere, at least not any time soon and that this is merely a chance to explore Scola and Nina’s relationship in a different way. When Nina was revealed to be moving to San Diego, there was no telling where things could be going for her and Scola, as well as their son, Dougie. And after the several cast exits the show has had in recent years, I appreciate the Boyd seems to understand why viewers would have questions.

Throughout the years, Nina and Scola have been through a lot, both as a couple and individually. While fans haven’t seen much of them since FBI: Most Wanted was canceled, we have been getting small updates here and there. Plus, VanSanten returned last season for the much-anticipated Scolina wedding. There's no telling how the relationship will progress, given they're working on opposite sides of the country and trying to raise their son together. I, for one, am eager to see how it plays out.

Also, even if there aren’t any plans to move Scola to San Diego in the near future, that isn’t stopping potential Scolina spinoff ideas. When asked by CinemaBlend if FBI could expand with another spinoff centered on Scola and Nina in San Diego, VanSanten said she was already campaigning for a new series. Unsurprisingly, Boyd reiterated his intention to stay with the Mothership. But, if we do eventually see Scola leaving 26 Fed, it would be fun to follow the fan-favorite couple in California.

I’m excited to see what FBI has planned for this next Scolina obstacle, and as long as Boyd is not leaving the series any time soon, I’ll be fine. All in all, fans should really stay tuned in as Season 9 continues. The show returns with a new episode on Monday, November 30, at 8 p.m. ET on CBS, streaming the next day on Paramount+.

#3605. GTA 6 can run at 60fps on Xbox Series X if you use a glitch, but there's a catch

Grand Theft Auto 6 runs at 30 frames-per-second across all the consoles it's currently available on, including the more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro. The game doesn't offer a 60fps performance mode or an option to unlock the frame-rate, but one industrious player has managed to do it anyway on Xbox.

Reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6's frame-rate on Series X. Their hack relied on the Xbox's rarely-discussed Quick Resume feature, which lets you park multiple games in memory and switch between them without having to re-load each game.

In a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch. For starters, you're going to need a 120Hz monitor display or TV, as the glitch requires adjusting refresh rates.

First, you need to limit Xbox to display at 60Hz under the console Settings menu. Then, you start GTA 6 (version 01.002.001), wait until the six-star logo appears and then go back to Xbox Settings to change the refresh rate to 120Hz.

Before you return to GTA 6, the final step requires launching another game on your console. This has to be a cold boot, meaning the game shouldn't already be running parked in Quick Resume.

After the second game launches, you now need to use Quick Resume to resume playing GTA 6, which is when you're going to notice the higher frame-rate. The Reddit user said the game could reach 90-plus FPS at certain moments.

Unfortunately, the user also discovered that game-speed appears to be tied to frame-rate in GTA 6, at least when it comes to certain gameplay animations and when performing certain actions. "I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more," Meowwie64 wrote. Incidentally, cutscenes do not appear to be affected by this issue, so they run at their normal speed.

As much as a 30fps frame-rate makes GTA 6 feel less smooth and potentially less enjoyable to play compared to 60fps or higher, none of the current-generation consoles are capable of delivering frame-rates beyond that. Tech experts Digital Foundry recently explained why even the PS5 Pro isn't powerful enough to run the game at 60fps or even 40fps.

#3603. Nvidia makes stunning decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO

"I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment."

Gaming tech giant Nvidia has decided to reinstate Jensen Huang as its president and CEO, despite allegedly saying it wouldn't, and despite a string of extramarital affairs and investigations into alleged bullying, workplace harassment, and humiliation.

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's Chair Harvey C. Jones announced on behalf of the Nvidia's board today - the same person reported as saying the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

"We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's chief financial officer."

In the same press release, Huang said he was "honoured" to return to the company "at the beginning of a new industrial revolution". "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said.

However, the investigation into one of Huang's extramarital affairs - the one with the person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy - will "proceed to conclusion". The company also said it formed a "National Security and Export Control Committee", with independent directors, in relation to this.

Huang resigned on 12th November a few days after his affair with the alleged Chinese spy came to light. Two subsequent affairs - both said to be with Nvidia employees and therefore his subordinates - were unearthed not long after, putting increased pressure on Huang and Nvidia.

Since his departure, Nvidia stock has tanked, and as news of his reinstatement spreads around the world, it has sharply recovered again.

It's GTA 6's world, and we're just living in it. Rockstar's latest release is an astonishing technical achievement to behold, confounding even developers working on big-budget games like Naughty Dog's Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet. It's been 13 long years since GTA 5, but seeing the staggering advancements in visual detail, depth of interactivity, and overall scale in GTA 6, you'd think it's been even longer. And yet, CD Projekt Red says we'll see a similar technical leap in The Witcher 4 compared to The Witcher 3, which came out in 2015.

During the Q&A portion of CDPR's latest earnings call, joint-studio CEO Michał Nowakowski fields a question about GTA 6 and whether The Witcher fans can expect a similar improvement from The Witcher 4. He says the team at CDPR "did look at [GTA 6]" and "did see the differences," and "we believe there's gonna be a comparable leap between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

"It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you can expect us to make a much bigger jump between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4," says Nowakowski.

There aren't many (read: any) studios with GTA 6's budget, which of course is supplied by Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive, but CDPR definitely has the resources to craft huge, visually stunning worlds packed with detail and complex systems that rival today's most expansive AAA games. Cyberpunk 2077 is the most recent example, but even 11 years on, The Witcher 3 absolutely holds up to modern open-world standards.

We're still a couple of years out from The Witcher 4's estimated 2028 release, but there's every reason to believe it'll make The Witcher 3 look downright dated, even after its recent remaster. Whether it'll truly mark a leap comparable to what Rockstar managed from GTA 5 to GTA 6 is a very different question we'll have to wait to answer.

Ciri in The Witcher 4 is "far more hot-headed" than Geralt, CD Projekt Red lead says, and "you are much more deeply involved in the story through her personal perspective"

Hailee Steinfeld just became a mama earlier this year when her and her husband Josh Allen welcomed their daughter in the spring. It was just confirmed that she’s got not one but two projects among upcoming 2026 movies – now that the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer showed Kate Bishop among the massive roster of heroes. But will her new starring role in her daughter’s life change how she approaches Hollywood going forward?

Most new mothers have to ask themselves the question of how work might change their lives once they become one. Here’s what Steinfeld said about it when it was posed to her by Entertainment Tonight:

I guess I’ve always made projects with the thought in my mind somewhere in there, maybe not necessarily at the front of it, but that like, I’ll get to share this with my family someday.

The beginning of Steinfeld’s answer reminds me how she famously decided to explore her own mixed heritage roots when she got to play Mary in Sinners. The actress said that the research for that role was looking into her family history, and that brought her closer to her mother and her grandfather, who account for the Filipino and African American side of her ancestry. These days she’s going to also think of her daughter too when she picks jobs, too. As Steinfeld said herself:

And now, I do feel like maybe moving forward that’ll be something I strongly take into account. But, the fact that [Hexed] was the first thing that came into my life and the first project that she is really a part of is really special.

Steinfeld’s latest movie is Walt Disney Animation’s latest, Hexed, which is all about a mother and her teen daughter at its core against a backdrop of a world of witches. The 29-year-old has shared before that the role came at a time where a story about “an overprotective mother makes a hell of a lot more sense to me” than it would have before this phase of her life.

In the movie, Steinfeld plays Billie, a misfit teenager who finds out she’s been a witch her whole life, but that her powers have been concealed by her mom with a bracelet. Rashida Jones voices the role of her mother along with Jodie Foster playing an evil witch named Celeste and Walton Goggins playing a three-eyed cat named Beef Roger. Hexed has earned positive reactions ahead of its release this Wednesday, November 25.

Outside of her latest role, Steinfeld is confirmed to reprise her role as Kate Bishop in Avengers: Doomsday, hitting theaters on December 18. Then we’ll hear her voice again as Gwen Stacy/Spider-Gwen in Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse coming out on June 18. We’re so curious what’s next for Steinfeld in her new mom era! For now, she’s staying booked and busy even as she enjoys some much-deserved time off with her baby daughter, Harper Haize Allen.

#3600. Chatting With People In GTA Online About Why They’re Not Playing GTA 6: ‘$80 Is Too Much For Me, Bro’

Grand Theft Auto 6 is the biggest video game on console right now. Everyone in my life, even people who don’t normally play these kinds of games, is booting up GTA 6 and spending hours exploring Vice City. But what about the people still playing GTA Online? What do they think of the newest entry which, for the time being, remains single-player? I dropped back into Rockstar’s existing multiplayer juggernaut a few days after GTA 6‘s launch to check out the vibes and ask people how they were feeling. The answers varied, but a surprisingly common response was that they were still playing GTA Online because they just couldn’t afford to buy GTA 6 right now.

GTA 5‘s live-service platform is still be very popular in 2026, but when I returned recently following the launch of GTA 6, it was definitely emptier than usual. I hopped into different sessions looking for players who were actually chatting on the mic, and found most lobbies to not be anywhere near close to full. In fact, many had only a few players hanging out in lobbies that support up to 30. I also ended up back in the same sessions again and again, which is not something that usually happens in GTA Online. And the sessions I landed in were filled with mostly low-level players and kids. A lot of the high-level kings and queens of GTA Online were missing. I assume they were chilling in Vice City.

One of the first people I spoke to was one of these GTA Online kids. They sounded no older than 12, and when I asked if they had played GTA 6, they told me no. I asked why and was told: “It sucks, bro.” I asked for more details, pretending I had yet to play it and was curious about it.

“It just sucks,” said the kid as he blew up a rival CEO. “I watched my cousin play it, bro, it just sucks. Likeâ¦it has good graphics, but GTA Online is more fun. It just sucks. That’s all I’m going to say about it, bro.â

Another player, who sounded a bit older, replied that “GTA 6 was shit” and that all the critics got “paid to glaze it.” Then he blew up the kid who said it sucked, and they started yelling at each other. At one point, the younger kid almost sounded like they were crying. It was awkward. Later, I ended up back in that session, and the kid who may have been crying was still very mad. Nobody else was talking in that session, so I hopped to a new one.

Eventually, I found a high-level player who was happy to chat. According to him, he desperately wants to play GTA 6, but money is tight.

“I gotta wait until I get paid again, dude,” the player told me over voice chat. “Iâve been waiting years…I can wait longer. I’m pretending I’m in GTA 6 right now. This chick next to me is Lucia. Or maybe Mandy!Â  Well, not as hot as her.” He laughed, and I asked if he’d been watching videos of GTA 6 while waiting to get paid and actually play it.Â

“Oh yeah, I’ve seen videos. Dude, it looks phenomenal. I can’t wait, man. But like, until then I’m here in GTA Online pretending it’s Vice City.” More laughter.

GTA Online is a community of players who will kill you in a heartbeat with a giant tank or flying car, but won’t ever say a single word to you before, during, or after. Shy little murderers. It’s been like this for years. So as I hopped from session to session, I also texted players via the in-game phone. It’s clunky, but I did get a few replies from people more willing to chat via text.

One person I texted, a level 7 player, confirmed that they just started playing GTA Online that very night. When I asked about GTA 6, they said they wanted to play, but it costs too much. So instead, the game’s historic launch inspired them to go back and finally give GTA Online a try. They had owned GTA 5 for a bit now and decided to kill time waiting for GTA 6 by making money in GTA Online. Another person I texted in-game simply told me GTA 6 looked boring and dumb. They apparently had no interest in playing it. Another player simply texted back, “$80 is too much for me, bro.”

In a different session, I found a gamer who claimed that everything they’d seen about GTA 6 made the game look “bad.”

“I don’t know, dude, seems boring,” said the player who sounded around my age. “Like I don’t wanna buy flowers for a girl and fix shit, bro. I wanna kill people and steal shit.” A moment later, that player yelled in anger as he was blown up by someone who was running around killing anyone they spotted with a flying motorcycle.Â

As I wrapped up my time back in GTA Online, I heard more kids yelling at each other about stealing drugs or something. In the background, I heard one kid yell out that he was going to invite someone else. The kid he was going to invite began screaming and crying in the background. “I don’t want to play GTA 5 ONLINE!”

Another person joked that he must want to play GTA 6 instead. And then he added: “My parents won’t buy GTA 6 for me because it’s, like, filled with boobs and shit.”

After playing GTA Online again and chatting with more people over voice and text, what I learned is that while some players are staying away from GTA 6 because of silly complaints about it being woke, the vast majority of players either don’t care about that or have no idea some online are complaining about that crap. Instead, the real reason most of them aren’t playing GTA 6 is simply that they don’t have the money to buy it right now. And many of them really want to play it.Â  That sucks for them, but it’s good news for Take-Two and Rockstar. GTA 6 is already selling incredibly well, and if my time in GTA Online has revealed one thing, it’s that even more people are going to be buying it soon once they can afford it.

#3599. GTA 6 just got a patch that fixed a progression bug on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S

Rockstar just issued a new patch for GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, targeting a few issues players have been reporting since the game launched last Thursday (19th November).

The 23rd November patch for the game deploys seven major fixes for the game, including a pretty significant bug that prevented phone calls not triggering at certain points, resulting in a scenario where you could be locked out of progressing the game. The official update is titled 'version 01.002.002', and its weighs in at different sizes on different consoles: it's 603.8 MB on PS5, and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X/S.

Thanks to an update on the Rockstar website, you can read all of the updates that arrive with the latest pathc below.

There have been a few fairly high-profile cases of the autosave not working as the developer intended, leading to a few cases of streamers losing plenty of real-world time thanks to unpredictable auto-save behaviour. JasonTheWeen lost 12 hours of progress on the PS5, for example.

But there's one issue here the developer hasn't addressed: vignetting. Plenty of players have taken to online communities to complain about the vignette effect that pops into the game - theoretically to help with motion smoothing and various grapihcal elements as the game runs in 30FPS. THe effect is worsened when you're fatigued, hungry, or have some other status effect, but it is present quite a lot of the time, too. Most of the responses to a tweet about the patch posted by the Rockstar Support account reference the vignetting in GTA 6, and the developer has issued no response at the time of writing.

The leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recreate GTA 6 on PC, have quit the project, although others are still trying to carry it on.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Just a day after Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker Cyberleek released the executable for the near-complete Xbox build of the game they dropped on Friday, at least two of the leads of Leonida, the biggest and best-known effort to recompile it to run on PC, have called it quits—seemingly under pressure from Take-Two and Rockstar.

The release of the exe made the pirated Xbox build effectively complete, and that opened the door for recomp projects to do their thing—that is, to leverage AI to quickly whip up a version of the game that will run on PC. Some hackers estimated it could be done within a week; Shayder, one of the lead developers on the Leonida project, said on X that followers could "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon."

In a separate message on the Leonida Discord, Shayder tempered expectations a bit, writing that "it will take at least a week" to come up with something playable on PC. During a subsequent livestream, however, the team was seemingly able to get the GTA 6 splash screen to come up on PC, although it crashed after that. It sure seemed like things were moving ahead quickly.

But then things began moving quickly in a different direction. "I quit guys. I’m sorry," NotRexed, apparently the head of the project, posted last night on X. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can’t control so I’m stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity."

Later, they added, "Last post from me. I wanna clear things up. Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I’ve said before, I’m a 15 year old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye."

In a reply post, NotRexed stated explicitly that "Rockstar shut the server down," and shared an image of the copyright violation notice he'd received from Discord.

Shayder, who had previously predicted rapid progress on the Leonida effort following the release of the Xbox executable, took a more direct approach and simply deleted all of their X posts.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

This isn't necessarily the end of work to bring GTA 6 (in a probably not-great state) to PC via AI. Other such projects are underway, and there also appears to be an effort to carry on with Leonida: The website remains up, with a new name attached as owner, and there's at least one Discord server dedicated to it, although it appears a little less focused at this point than the original Leonida server. A new Github repository (NotRexed also deleted that) has been set up: It's "a continuation of NotRexed's Leonida project," according to a note on the project, which adds that "development continues here with its full commit history."

The advent of AI greatly simplifies and speeds up the work of bringing console games to PC (as long as you're not too picky about the quality), and that makes life tougher for companies that want to keep a lid on such projects. Still, it's not surprising that Take-Two and Rockstar are going hard on it: In the past, Take-Two has moved aggressively to shut down GTA 5 mod projects, an effort that culminated in its acquisition of the biggest and best of them. I've reached out to Take-Two for more information on the takedown and will update if I receive a reply.

#3597. Dawn of War 4's newest trailer teases the appearance of a fan-favourite character in the game's post-launch DLC

As Dawn of War 4's December release date inches ever closer, a new trailer appears to have teased a fan-favourite character's inclusion in the RTS's first post-launch DLC.

The trailer, which covers the Commander Edition of Dawn of War 4, includes a breakdown of all the extra stuff packed in alongside this version of the game. This includes the digital soundtrack, three-days of early-access to the game, and the story prologue. It'll also include the Aftermath post-launch DLC too, with its dedicated campaign and new playable faction.

Now, ever since the Aftermath DLC was announced, people have speculated it would be chaos-focused. The design of the DLC logo is black with a gold trim, an often-used colour scheme for the faction. However, which sort of Chaos was left up to debate. That is, until this trailer, where the answer is seemingly given away with a cheeky tease.

In its final few seconds, the trailer shows a pair of glowing yellow mechanical eyes peering out from a gloomy background. This was quickly identified as almost-certainly Vashtorr the Arkifane, a relatively new addition to Warhammer 40,000 and a fan-favourite baddie all around.

Vashtorr as a character has been getting a lot of love ever since his introduction in 2023. It was then, during the Arks of Omen campaign for the tabletop game, that he played a central part in the narrative event bridging the game's 10th and 11th edition. Since then he was the main antagonist of Boltgun 2, and was central in the 2025 novel Achmagos.

What this means for Dawn of War 4 is that, if he is a commander of Chaos forces, expect a lot of machinery and demon engines on his side. That's kind of his whole deal. Whether that means he's paired with tech-focused Dark Mechanicum as a sort of mirror to the Adeptus Mechanicus faction already in the game, or if he'll come alongside Chaos Space Marines to better reflect the Dark Angels / Blood Ravens remains to be seen. It could also be a mix of both! We'll have to wait and see.

Dedicated servers complicate the "without a multiplayer subscription" part

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"The crossplay era for Terraria starts here," declares developer Re-Logic in a new Steam post announcing "Phase One" of the iconic sandbox adventure game's crossplay rollout.

Terraria's new-fangled crossplay, which allows players on different platforms to share multiplayer worlds and progress, comes with a few caveats, but it's a big step forward nonetheless.

"Starting today, for most people using the same Wi-Fi/wired network you will be able to play together with any device which has v1.4.6 Terraria, without a multiplayer subscription," Re-Logic explains. "Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, Android, Apple, PC, Mac; if you're on the same network, in most circumstances your games should be able [to] see each other in the Local section of the NEW multiplayer menu."

What about online multiplayer for distant players? That's the focus of the second phase of crossplay. "This first phase of Crossplay is all about making it easier to play together on the local network," the devs reiterate.

Additionally, options for joining dedicated PC servers are a little complicated. To join on PlayStation or Xbox, you will need an online subscription, as at that point you're going through Sony and Microsoft's infrastructure.

"Switch cannot connect to privately hosted dedicated servers, either Local or Online. This is due to security and safety restrictions required by Nintendo for the platform," Re-Logic adds.

"If you are running a dedicated server on one of the server hosting services, the IP or web address can be manually input with the + Add Server button at the bottom of the multiplayer menu. Just type in the details. This will add an entry to the Server section which will remember the details for future sessions."

The full 1.4.6 patch notes add a bit more color. For example, Steam players can now invite their friends directly in-game "without opening the overlay." The devs snuck in a few balance changes, too, with Heavy variants of Armored Skeletons (very important) having their health rebalanced for Expert and Master modes.

As Terraria sells over 70 million copies, devs are done with promising final updates and say they'll "continue beyond 1.4.6"

Disneyland live entertainment is few and far between as of late, which is a shame considering the Anaheim theme park used to boast some of the best shows. On November 21st, one of the last and most beloved nighttime shows, Fantasmic, went up in flames for the second time in three short years. With two incidents and Disney’s desire to cut back on live entertainment, I’m really starting to worry about the future of the show.

The fire reportedly broke out during Fantasmic’s second performance of the night shortly before the show’s finale. While the Mark Twain finale was able to go on, flames can be seen behind the boat on the small stage set up on Tom Saywer Island. Guests at the park were quick to pull out their phones and film the growing flames as the Mark Twain, full of classic Disney characters, made its way around the river. Take a look:

Here’s the Mark Twain Riverboat running during Fantasmic last night with the fire behind it. This happened during the 10:30PM show https://t.co/bMcOZ6z0PtNovember 22, 2026

The last two minutes of the show were canceled, and guests were asked to vacate the viewing area while the fire department handled the blaze. Thankfully, the fire was small compared to the 2023 incident that turned the Maleficent dragon animatronic into a giant fireball and forever changed the show. There’s been no word on the extent of the damage this time around, but considering the show was back Sunday night it safe to assume that nothing was affected and no cast members were harmed, thankfully.

Two fiery incidents are definitely a cause for concern, and with Disneyland executives’ history of scaling back entertainment to cut costs, I can’t help but worry about the show’s fate. After all, Fantasmic boasts a large cast of incredible performers and several floating units. Plus water screens, projectors, and fireworks. I’m no expert, but I’m willing to bet it’s one of the most costly attractions at Disneyland. Not to mention, the show is still feeling the loss of the Maleficent Dragon, which makes the battle between Mickey and Maleficent lackluster.

While I don’t think Disneyland would end the show without also announcing a replacement, I do think Disney fans should prepare themselves. After all, Disney fans aren’t known for taking new changes well. Just look at the uproar that happened when it was announced Dinosaur would close to make room for a new Indiana Jones attraction at Disney World.

Disneyland has been having a rough go at things this month. On the first day of the holiday season, the Anaheim theme park’s iconic fake snow was accidentally turned on during a rainstorm, creating a mess. Back in October, Frontierland experienced widespread flooding. With park tickets being so expensive, it’s unfortunate to see cracks in Disneyland’s magic, but not even the mouse can control the weather or unexpected fires.

Handling Mass Effect 3âs divergent endings was one thing, but what about the beloved crewmates players wouldnât have seen since Mass Effect 3? Catherynne M. Well, it sounds like BioWare was considering those questions, but Valente stops short of confirming they would have appeared.

âI think the best way to answer your question is to say that any character who physically could survive, we considered allowing to survive into the new game and made decisions on them,â she wrote. âWe thought about all the things you’d have wanted us to think about, and I hope you do believe that, because it’s the truth. Everyone in that room loved those characters, or loved to hate them, as much as any fan. We took each and every one of them and their fates very seriously.â

Elsewhere, Valente was asked if players would have been able to learn what happened to squadmates after the Reaper War in Mass Effect 3, and she says that part of her work on Universe was to write those fates and variations, and that players would have been able to learn what happened in the 600 years between.

Asked if she had âheadcanonsâ about the fates of those characters, she replied, âNo, darling, I don’t have headcanons about those fates, I have canon-canons. I know you’d have been able to find out about them because one of my jobs was to write all those fates and their possible variations all then submitted to the room, workshopped with everyone, and sent to higher-ups for approval. #3593. God of War Laufey's Faye actor jumps from games to live-action, as Amazon casts Deborah Ann Woll in upcoming series

After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series.

Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first showed up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey.

Amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir.

Earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course.

There's no release date yet for the show, but it's said to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back.

Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

"We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica said at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon."

While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back, too.

"Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad."

Gravity Well, founded in 2020 as an "anti-crunch" game studio, lost its funding earlier this year and wasn't able to find a new backer.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

Gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy said at the time.

"That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good."

But like so many other ambitious new studios launched around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it said was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain."

A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS) says the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation."

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. "Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we're going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you're a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation."

The announcement concludes with an invitation to publishers and investors to reach out if they're interested in supporting the project.

#3591. Activision calls Banjo-Kazooie one of its "iconic gaming franchises," raising hopes for long-awaited new game

Banjo-Kazooie - the iconic Rare platformer starring an absent-minded bear and the sassy red bird he carries in a backpack - has been on hiatus for years, but a new Activision job listing has raised hopes for a new game.

In a LinkedIn post advertising a 'Product Manager, Emergent Franchises' role, the publisher wrote that it's "home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, and now… Halo, Age of Empires, Sea of Thieves, and Banjo Kazooie."

"Become part of the team working on building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises," the listing goes on. "As a Product Manager, you will serve as the publishing product lead for an upcoming premium console & PC title, driving the product from concept to launch."

If you're scratching your brain trying to remember when Activision took control of the beloved platformer, well, it happened during Xbox's last massive internal shakeup. Amid the mass layoffs and studio divestments, Xbox also made some drastic changes to its corporate structure - Halo, World's Edge and Rare were all slotted under Activision's supervision.

Rare's 40-year history includes almost too many notable games to list, but the internal rejig presumably put Activision in control of games like Conker, Viva Pinata and Killer Instinct, alongside the aforementioned pirate hit Sea of Thieves and Banjo-Kazooie.

The job post is by no means confirmation that a new Banjo-Kazooie game is in development, but it is the only series named here that can be considered dormant, perhaps hinting that Activision has plans to revive it down the line. Crash Bandicoot 4 and Spyro: A Realm Beyond lay out a pretty good blueprint for its return, I think.

The last properly new game in the series came 18 years ago with the Xbox 360's Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts, a surprisingly good physics-driven vehicle construction sandbox.

Since then, Banjo and Kazooie showed up as a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros Ultimate. More recently, a fan-made PC port and an Evercade Double Pack have kept the series chugging.

Composer Grant Kirkhope was slightly more hopeful about the prospect of a Banjo-Threeie back in September. "I do know of like three companies that have actually physically pitched to Microsoft or to Rare about making another Banjo-Kazooie game, and I don't think anyone was successful," he said at the time.

"This game should probably be capped at 30fps"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Rockstar's decision to cap GTA 6 at 30fps remains a controversial one, especially after we spent much of the PS5 and Xbox Series X generation getting used to 60fps gameplay on consoles. But if you thought the recent 60fps glitch discovered on Xbox would be a quick piece of salvation, you should probably recalibrate your expectations. As it turns out, it's really more of a 36fps glitch.

That's according to new analysis from Digital Foundry, which has put the supposed 60fps glitch through its paces. On one level, it's true – you can get GTA 6 to run at 60fps. But that's only if you take a plane up into the air, well away from any roving NPCs on the map, and point the camera directly at the sky.

In real gameplay, removing the frame rate cap is still going to leave you with a "mean average" of "about 36 to 37 frames per second," based on testing of the first hour of the game. In other words, "Rockstar isn't keeping anything amazing from you." That's the sort of awkward, variable frame rate that's a lot more unpleasant than a steady 30 frames per second, and DF's analysts agree that "this game should probably be capped at 30fps."

That's not even counting the part where GTA 6 currently runs at an increased speed based on the frame rate, but that's likely just an artifact of the glitch rather than a suggestion that there's some underlying issue with the game. "Ultimately this shouldn't be reflecting on the quality of the code itself," DF's Richard Leadbetter observes. "Obviously there are going to be versions in the future of Grand Theft Auto 6 that will be running at faster than 30fps."

Just don't expect those future versions to run on current-gen consoles. Our first taste of 60fps GTA 6 will likely come on PC, though whether it'll first arrive through an official port or a fan-made PC version remains to be seen.

For six seasons now, Abbott Elementary fans have faithfully watched the relationship between Janine Teagues (Quinta Brunson) and Gregory Eddie (Tyler James Williams) progress. The pair have gone from good friends to committed lovers over the past several years and, now, it seems we’re on the cusp of a proposal. Many viewers are hoping an engagement will come during the Disneyland-set 100th episode that’ll air amid the 2026 TV schedule. I’d love that as well, but I also have a question about two other characters.

Gregory and Janine are, of course, the core couple on Abbott, but plenty of other romantic relationships amongst characters have been highlighted as well. As we anticipate what lies ahead for Janine and Gregory, I can’t help but wonder what the future holds for Ava Coleman and O’Shon, who’ve been dating since Season 4. I’ve enjoyed seeing their relationship develop as well as the funny moments that have resulted from that. With that, it’s hard not to wonder what the long-term plan for them might look like.

It’s clear that the affable O’Shon (Matthew Law) and Abbott’s diva of a principal Ava (Critics Choice winner Janelle James) are on steady footing after some initial growing pains. At this point, the pair have not only vacationed together, but they’ve also reached the point where they can throw a party as a couple. (That Halloween shindig they held this season was fantastic). Some may think it’s a bit early to consider a proposal for these two, but I don’t think it’s wild to think it could happen by the end of Season 6.

Gregory first expressed interest in proposing to Janine at the end of Season 5, which was about two years after the two finally got together. Ava and O’Shon will be reaching that mark later in the sixth season and, while great TV couples have different timelines, I could see O’Shon popping the question soon. Plus, given how encouraging O’Shon has been amid Gregory’s attempts to propose, who’s to say the former doesn’t want that for himself sometime in the near future?

Of course, I’m not saying anyone needs to be jumping the broom by the end of this season. I just wouldn’t mind seeing one or two engagements by the time Abbott’s finale rolls around next spring. That may seem like a long shot for Ava and O’Shon right now, but I’m feeling very good about Janine and Gregory’s chances of hitting that milestone.

The True Story That Inspired Abbott Elementary’s Choice To Move The School Into A Mall

Gregory has been trying to orchestrate the right moment to present Janine with a ring. During the show’s latest episode, “Competition,” he attempted to land a reservation at a popular Italian restaurant, where he could propose. Ironically, that plan became moot once Abbott’s Step Team punched their ticket to Disneyland, and Janine informed her man that they’d serve as chaperones on the trip. So it now seems like a given that Gregory will attempt to propose while he and his lady are in “The Happiest Place On Earth.”

What’s more is that the pressure is going to be on, as Janine is aware of her beau’s intention to pop the question (thanks to a major slip-up on Ava’s part). So the pressure is really on for Eddie to craft the perfect proposal. The Disneyland episode could indeed present him the right situation to do just that and, if Gregory does pull it off in great fashion, it might set a bit of a bar for O’Shon to clear if he eventually takes that step.

We’ll just have to wait and see how it plays out when Abbott Elementary airs its hundredth episode on Wednesday, December 2 at 8:30 p.m. ET on ABC. Fans can also stream the show the next day with a Hulu subscription.

#3587. Deltarune Chapter 6 is playable "from the beginning to the end," Toby Fox says, but the RPG's final part has "only just started"

"Unlike every other chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time."

Toby Fox has given eager fans an update on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

"Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)"

While the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing."

Deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox said he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible."

And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

"Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way"

"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence."

Deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two launched together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

We don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

One of the cars Randy wants in GTA 6 is the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular—and don't let the name fool you, its a slick and speedy ride that'll you'll be tempted to keep for yourself.

But Randy doesn't know the locations of many of the cars on his wishlist, and can't point you to the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular: you just need to keep an eye out for it. Luckily, we spotted it ourselves, so just follow the simple steps below to find it.

Head to Belville: It's a town in Leonard County, in the central eastern part of the map, a bit south of Lake Leonida and north of La Perle.

In the northern edge of Belville there's a little cluster of four homes laid out almost in an X pattern. The southernmost home of that cluster has a garage you can break into. Once you open the garage door, you'll see the white Ocelot Bloodless Jugular.

You'll need the key cloner to get in, which I assume you already have since you're doing jobs for Randy. No need to worry about the tracker, it's a standard one so it won't transmit your location to the cops. You still don't want to dawdle, because the owner of the car has a gun and he's not afraid to use it. He'll start shooting if he sees you boost the car.

Randy will pay you $10,615 for the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular. He'll pay an extra $5,000 if you bring it to him in pristine condition.

#3585. Modders already have GTA 6 running on PC, after CyberLeek released a full Xbox build of the game

A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought. After suddenly returning last week with a near-full build of the Xbox version, notorious leaker CyberLeek has now posted the missing piece they intentionally held back: the game's executable (.exe) file.

"The exe is out. Always free. An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit. "The torch passes to the open source re-comp and emulation projects."

Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.

In just a matter of hours, modders - with the help of Claude AI - managed to turn the leaked Xbox build into a PC port, of sorts. In this Reddit video, you can see the game boot up to the initial setup before hitting a black screen. The build is clearly not yet playable, though Eurogamer has not directly verified those claims.

Shayder, one of the lead developers on Project Leonida, said in a since-deleted post on X that we should "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." On the project's Discord server, they later clarified that it could take about a week for the build to reach a playable state on PC.

As for CyberLeek, the leaker is still soliciting donations for a secret project "for the gamers", adding in the build's readme file, "Nobody has to give anything, and every release stays free either way. But every donation is a vote for more of this, and so is every trade of the token."

Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6, but the company has historically released its games on PC several months after their console debut. In October, a report said GTA 6's PC version would arrive in the first quarter of 2027, an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases.

These latest recompilation efforts, however, may force Rockstar to speed up development of the PC version. Though the recompiled build may never reach the level of quality or stability of an official port, many of those eager to play the game on PC likely wouldn't care.

A death that really puts things in perspective.

Warning: There is discussion of suicide in this story.

It’s been seven months since Storage Wars star Darrell Sheets died by suicide in his home in Arizona, and it sounds like the other stars of the show, like Brandi Passante, are still, understandably, processing his death. Season 19 of the reality show kicks off on the 2026 television schedule on November 28th, and ahead of its premiere, Passante talked about Sheets’ passing and how it has affected both her personally and the production of the show.

Sheets left the show as a full-time cast member in 2019 after suffering a heart attack. He remained in contact with the rest of the cast, including Passante, and he made occasional guest appearances after retiring. In a discussion with TV Insider, Passante talked about how his death has affected the show, including how the rest of the cast work with each other:

It definitely changed the dynamic with everybody. We’re all a little softer and kinder to each other since that happened. There was a lot of beef and animosity before between most of us. Some things are not worth fighting.

Sheets’ death, like so many do, really seems to have put things in perspective for the rest of the cast. Their rivalries are what make the show so endlessly watchable, but in the end, they have known each other for almost two decades now, so something like this is bound to change things. Sheets’ manner of death is also a particularly difficult thing to endure, according to Passante:

I’ve endured a lot of deaths in that same manner over the years, and that is just a grief that, you know, kind of sticks with you. It’s not like losing somebody to cancer or a heart attack. It’s something that you think maybe you could have helped prevent. It’s one of those difficult deaths that you never can really wrap your head around.

Anyone who has lost a loved one to suicide knows how Passante feels. It can feel completely helpless. For her part, Passante is doing what she can, including checking in on Sheets’ son, Brandon, who was by his father’s side at all the auctions until Darrell left the show. Passante said:

I talk to [his son] Brandon a lot now. We didn’t really chat much over the years when they left. We would talk every once in a while during holidays or something, but now I just try to keep tabs. He sends me little messages maybe once a week. I just like to check in on him because it’s a hard thing to swallow. I’m sure that he’s missing his dad.

Ultimately, Passante summed it up quite succinctly by saying simply, “It sucks.”

There has been a lot of drama on Storage Wars over the years, and while much of it is contrived for the show, behind-the-scenes has been filled with drama, too. Passante has been in the middle of some of it when she divorced her long-time partner in life and in business, Jarrod Schulz, after Season 13 of the show. There has been nothing like the tragedy that befell Sheets, though, and keeping everything in perspective is important.

If the race to get GTA 6 running on PC looks like a mess, that's because it is.

Recomp forerunner Leonida and its rapidly expanding Discord community have seemingly been nuked from orbit after developer Rockstar Games decided that's the only way to be sure, but Leonida is just one of many sloppy efforts to convert a leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 into a playable PC version. These projects are universally powered, if not majority-piloted, by AI tools like Claude and Google's Antigravity, which are also behind the recent game recomp boom that even caught Microsoft's attention.

The large community attracted by the unprecedented success and popularity of GTA 6 has made this vibe-coded game explosion clearer than ever. It's also highlighted the glaring difference between the people using AI to expedite programming and the people asking AI to do everything for them.

The Xbox build and executable shared by notorious GTA 6 leaker and crypto grifter Cyberleek chummed the waters. Now, tons of people, some of whom couldn't get a blue square to move around on-screen without AI assistance, are chucking GTA 6 files into AI tools and telling machines to cobble them together. The results have been mixed.

Before the Leonida Discord was taken down, I'd become a regular reader of its feeds and updates. It's hard to overstate just how AI-dependent many contributors in this space are; across the board, would-be GTA 6 porters openly admit to having no technical experience being holding carrots in front of AI agents.

Twitter use Chasm, who's chronicled GTA 6 PC efforts over the past few days, logged just some of the ways that GTA 6 vibe coders interact with AI. "I've gathered some of the prompts I've found from watching dev streams. No this isn't a joke," he says.

We begin with a classic, seemingly fed to Google's Antigravity: "Make no mistakes."

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"Keep finding more stuff and working and pushing," implores another promt.

"You need [to do] one thing at a time not a little bit of everything," reads one.

In a Twitter post, former Leonida project lead NotRexed said: "I let Fable 7.2 work overnight with just one prompt: Get GTA 6 running on my PC. I woke up the next morning with the game fully running at 240fps."

Imagine a chef taking a microwave meal out of its cardboard packaging, placing the plastic container on a cold griddle, and then waiting for food to happen, confident that they at least cut steam vents in the cover. These are the people – rather, a non-trivial number of the people – currently trying to get GTA 6 running on PC.

I'm reminded of March comments from Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Rockstar owner Take-Two. Zelnick said the idea of AI making something as complex and high-quality as GTA 6 is "laughable," dismissing the purported ability of gen AI tools replacing creators.

"The notion that somehow new tools would allow an individual to push a button and generate a hit, and market a hit, and bring it to many millions of consumers around the world… It's a laughable notion," he said. You might get a song back if you prompt an AI tool to generate one, he added, but "I defy you to listen to it more than once."

You can't just tell a computer to make GTA 6, Zelnick argued. Yet here we are. Computer, work faster, make no mistakes, and make this game run on PC.

"The community aspect of decompilation has been broken" by a wave of low-effort AI slop, and now a major community tool is shutting down

Rupert Grint is the latest cast member from the Harry Potter films to join the Broadway run of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, right on the heels of Tom Felton's successful run. With Ron Weasley in tow, he's already fielding questions about whether Emma Watson and Danielle Radcliffe could be next to join the stage play.

The actor, who will reprise his role as Ron for the production, confirmed it would be his last time playing the character. As such, Collider wanted to know if there was a chance of his former famous co-stars joining. Grint didn't say definitively one way or another, but offered up this:

It would be fun. I don't know. I mean, it's obviously different for everyone. It was an intense time. When we finished, I really enjoyed stepping away and not really even thinking about it, because it was such an intense… I mean, it was enjoyable, and they looked after us, but it was a big part of us. So, yeah, maybe. I don't know. It'd be fun.

I'm sure the last thing Grint wanted to do was try to put the pressure on Radcliffe and Watson to say no, knowing the complicated thoughts both may have about returning. Daniel Radcliffe has been pretty adamant about refusing any opportunities to return, and Emma Watson has shied away from acting so much that there were rumors a few years back that she had retired.

People are always free to change their minds of course, and Rupert Grint is evidence of that. He initially said he'd only return if everyone else did, and now he's in a position where he's being asked whether his co-stars will join him onstage for Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. He talked about his return and how he felt immediately after the film franchise ended way back when:

Yeah. It's funny. It's interesting, going back. I spent so much time after finishing Potter kind of moving away from it and doing other things, which I've really enjoyed doing, but I think now it's a very different role in a very different context. And weirdly, it's kind of lined up that I'm the exact age of the character in that story, so it's just felt like a good time.

It does feel like a good time, what with a new Harry Potter TV show on the way. The series' arrival on the 2026 TV schedule will likely spark even more interest than usual in the franchise, and possibly encourage a lot of millennials craving nostalgia to see Grint back as Ron.

Timing aside, I'm sure it doesn't surprise anyone that actors love to work. For Rupert Grint, the return to being on stage pulls back to his start as a child actor, and that's going to be a great joy for him:

And I love New York and being on stage. It's been a while since I've done that, and it's a very important thing to me. It was my childhood, and I have a very strong connection to that character and that world. I think I'm not going to get many other opportunities to play him again. It probably is my last, and I think it'll be fun.

It should be fun, especially given what Ron Weasley is up to in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. He's running the joke shop Fred and George founded, while his wife Hermione is the literal Minister of Magic. As far as acting is concerned, it's more of a supportive role, but one that Rupert Grint will likely bring a special sparkle to.

I'm still waiting to see if Grint, Emma Watson, or Daniel Radcliffe will show up in the Potter TV series. Part of me thinks they'd do it for the fans, but at the same time, I could see them wanting the new cast to have a chance to do their own thing, without drawing attention to themselves. I guess all we can do is wait and see what happens!

Rupert Grint's run on Broadway in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child kicks off on February 2nd and will end on May 30th. I'm sure getting a ticket could be a struggle, but I'm eager to see what the demand will be for fans to see one of the core stars back in the franchise!

#3580. Microsoft reportedly looked into killing paid multiplayer for next-gen Xbox Helix consoles

A new report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.

"Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," says the Windows Central report. It goes on to note that this Xbox Live-free plan was iterated upon under Xbox's previous leadership, but with Asha Sharma's appointment as Xbox head in February, all that apparently changed. I guess she did promise "radically different business models", after all.

The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: new management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report. We've previously heard that Xbox's next-gen console could cost up to $1,800, with a handheld version coming in 2027 and a full release by holiday 2028 (a Helix console at $1,200 would mean a 50 percent increase on top of Series X's current price, for what it's worth). Sharma has stressed Helix will launch as "a family of devices" that will act as a bridge between PC and Xbox capable of playing games from both platforms.

If Xbox has, indeed, decided to scrap the idea of free online multiplayer access, it'll be a blow to the idealistic 'PC and Xbox' platform that Microsoft has been touting for the past few years: PC players do not need a subscription in order to access online modes, so - right out the gate - there will be a division between one group of players and the other. Perhaps this is why we've heard a little change in the tone of how Sharma and other Xbox bosses are talking about Helix more recently - these hints that the console will be a true PC-and-console hybrid have died down, and been replaced by insinuations that we'll see more of a traditional console with the "ability to play your PC games."

Xbox has been running Xbox Live as a service since 2002, when it launched on the original Xbox console. By 2005, it was split into gold and silver tiers to distinguish free players from those that paid. In 2023, the service was fully renamed Xbox Game Pass Core, looping in access to the base roster of Game Pass games with online play.

There are tons of unique and collectible weapons in GTA 6 but these are the best and easiest to snap up early in the game.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 has a ton of unique weapon variants all with their own names and mods. They're all special custom builds of stock guns and weapons with unique skins, but some of them are way more worth the trouble to hunt down than others. You'll find some of them easily—every Ammu-Nation has a unique gun sitting out for you to buy. The best unique weapons are a little more hidden. There are treasure hunts and easter eggs and a whole lot that you'll grab by fighting your way through a gang hideout.

The Assassin Nipper is at the south tip of the eastern island in the Permit Keys.

Use Focus Mode to find the hidden cache for the Assassin Nipper .38

This is the easiest unique weapon to grab right at the start of the game and totally worth the boat ride to grab it. There isn't even any combat to get to it, like many of these other uniques. The Assassin Nipper comes with a suppressor attachment, which is a really expensive mod to buy early in the game. Pick it up as soon as you've got free range in Key Lento from an old shipwreck in the Permit Keys near the military base location.

Another great Chapter 1 snag is this sniper rifle at a Kingfisher hideout. The combat to get it is minimal (don't get between that tiger and its prey) so it's easy to pick up early. It's a bolt action that can't equip a silencer, so it isn't exactly a stealth tool, but it can help Jason pick off gangsters in a hideout before even going inside. It comes with a stock and a basic dot sight.

A variant of the Vom Feur V5FC, found in Port Gellhorn at a Kolt gang hideout. It's up on the top floor of the motel by the La Cascara Motel safe, so you pretty much have to complete this illegal operation to grab it. I recommend coming up the south stairwell that's less guarded and hugging the outer walkways to get most of the way to the loot room by stealth. It's worth it though. The Scrapper is a silenced longarm SMG fairly early in the game with an extended mag and a flashy paint job.

This Duke Carbine variant doesn't have a suppressor but it is quite high accuracy for a full auto assault rifle with a heavy stock and 7" pistol barrel mod. The Kolt 556 is easier to smash and grab than the Scrapper, though. You've got to fight in and out of the Kolt stash house, but it's a small joint so it's not too hard to get away clean. It's in a gun case on a kitchen table near the safe full of pills.

Blade Runner 2099 has arguably been one of the most anticipated titles on the 2026 TV schedule, and there’s a good reason for that. Not only does it expand upon the classic science-fiction franchise, but it also has two capable leads in Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer (who do plenty of stunt work). The show debuts later this week, and reviews are finally starting to roll in. Having seen the show in its entirety for myself, I figured there would be high praise for the visuals, but I am surprised by one particular critique amongst critics.

If there’s anything to know about the Blade Runner universe, it’s that it has major dystopian vibes, and that particular aura is definitely present in 2099. The series continues to highlight a version of Los Angeles in the distant future that’s far from pristine. Surprisingly enough, though, it seems that the show is proving to be a little too dark for some pundits’ liking. Scott Collura of IGN praises the visual style of the series, though he takes issue with just how bleak the proceedings get:

Blade Runner 2099 is a disappointing continuation of the iconic series which leans too heavily into the dark and downbeat side of its future dystopia rather than finding ways to elevate its lead characters in that world. Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer are both miscast as a buddy-cop team that subsist on fear and mistrust and angst, while the more interesting characters don’t get nearly enough to do. While the production design, visual effects and overall look of the show are a wonder to behold, 2099 also leans so heavily into its creators’ own fandom at times that it can be distracting.

2099 – which, of course, takes place 50 years after 2017’s Blade Runner 2049 – sees Replicants having become the ruling class, while humans are treated like vermin. At the center of the story is Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human trying to escape her circumstances by posing as a Replicant Blade Runner. In the process of doing that, she is partnered with Olwen (Yeoh), a dying Replicant Runner. The story does indeed get dark, but I didn’t have much of an issue with it. As for The Guardian’s Rhik Samadder, though, he says:

If you’re a cyberpunk who mainlines ennui and likes watching actors you can’t see, speaking words you can’t hear, this show may well knock your fishnet socks off. But why spend this much time immersed in a doomed world, when you could open up a window and watch the real one? It’s live!

Samadder also notably calls the visuals both “impressive” and “oppressive” in a way. However, also mentioning that the series also “plunges us into a far darker world” than the Blade Runner movies (which don’t directly tie into 2099). Likewise, Aaron Pruner of CNET isn’t really a fan of the overly dark setting and aesthetic. In his somewhat mixed review, Pruner praises the show’s execution while also posing this question regarding the bleak vibe:

Could a little bit of levity help break up the monotony? Possibly. But, again, that would go against the grain of the Blade Runner franchise. And not for nothing, the original wasn’t at all funny, yet nuanced characters like Roy Batty (Rutger Hauer) and Pris (Daryl Hannah) brought life and color to the dreary, rain-slick streets of Ridley Scott’s original.

The darkness doesn’t seem to be deterring everyone, though, as Alison Herman of Variety has glowing thoughts on the show. Aside from praising Hunter Schafer, Herman also admires series creator Silka Luisa’s adherence to this storied continuity birthed by Philip K. Dick:

‘Blade Runner 2099’ dutifully incorporates the franchise’s visual and thematic touchstones. Despite the passage of time, computer screens still have the blocky, vintage look of early PCs; a psychotically violent replicant named Clotilde (Amy Lennox), an early convert to a cult of personality that promises her and Olwen’s kind eternal life, is a clear echo of Daryl Hannah’s cartwheeling Pris from the original film. ‘Blade Runner’ has always hewn to the beats of a detective noir, and over time, has acquired mainstays of its own that ‘2099’ dutifully nods to.

That’s definitely a big compliment, considering how beloved Ridley Scott’s original 1982 film is and how much critical praise Denis Villeneuve’s 2049 received. Still, not everyone is impressed. TVLine’s Dave Nemetz finds the sci-fi show to be overly bleak as well. Not only that, but he also isn’t too taken with the visuals like a number of others are:

We get it: The L.A. of the future is a rough scene. But there's no spark of joy or hope here to offset the bleakness... just more bleakness. ‘2099’ should at least provide some sci-fi eye candy, but the visuals are a disappointing rehash of the sleek, neon-soaked aesthetic of the original ‘Blade Runner.’

Although I can’t say I saw these critiques about the show’s vibe coming, I can’t blame others for not caring for its dark nature. To me, this kind of style is just baked into the DNA of the franchise, though I can admit that Blade Runner 2099 does delve into murkier territory at times. I’m curious as to how fans will feel when all eight episodes of the show become available for Prime Video subscription holders on November 25.
